claims.statement: According to legend she was a beautiful siren of the Rhine (Rin) who drew men from the rock bearing her name with her beauty and songs, causing shipwrecks and disasters.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Lorelei adalah siren cantik Sungai Rhein (Rin) yang memikat para lelaki dari batu karang bernama sama dengan kecantikan dan nyanyiannya, menyebabkan kapal karam dan bencana.
claims.quote: Según la leyenda, fue una hermosa sirena del río Rin que atraía a los hombres desde la roca que lleva su nombre con su belleza y sus cantos, causando naufragios y desastres.

claims.statement: Lorelei is a legendary figure of Germany (Germania).
claims.statement_id: Lorelei adalah tokoh legenda dari Jerman (Germania).
claims.quote: Lorelei è una figura leggendaria della Germania.

claims.statement: According to legend Lorelei was a lovely undine of the Rhine (Reno) who drew men with her song and looks, causing shipwrecks and misfortune; the rock where she appeared still bears her name.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Lorelei adalah ondina cantik Sungai Rhein (Reno) yang memikat para lelaki dengan nyanyian dan rupanya, menyebabkan kapal karam dan bencana; batu karang tempat ia menampakkan diri masih menyandang namanya.
claims.quote: Secondo la leggenda, Lorelei era una bellissima ondina del fiume Reno, che attirava a sé gli uomini col suo canto e con il suo aspetto, causando naufragi e sciagure.

claims.statement: She was believed to have first been a beautiful girl betrayed by the man she loved, who then threw herself from a cliff, unable to bear the pain.
claims.statement_id: Konon ia semula gadis cantik yang dikhianati lelaki yang dicintainya, lalu terjun dari tebing karena tak sanggup menanggung pedihnya.
claims.quote: Según se creía, originariamente era una hermosa muchacha que fue traicionada por el hombre al que amaba, tras lo cual se arrojó de un acantilado por no poder soportar el dolor.

claims.statement: Per the Turkish article, the legend says she wants revenge on sailors after the fisherman she loved deceived her.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Turki, legenda menyebut ia ingin membalas dendam kepada para pelaut setelah nelayan kekasihnya mengkhianatinya.
claims.quote: Efsaneye göre âşık olduğu balıkçının kendisini aldatması üzerine gemicilerden öç almak istemektedir.

claims.statement: To avenge his dead son, a nobleman sent soldiers immune to her charm to kill her; her father sent a horse of foam that took the nymph to the river depths, from which she never returned.
claims.statement_id: Untuk membalas kematian putranya, seorang bangsawan mengirim prajurit yang tahan pesona Lorelei untuk membunuhnya; ayahnya mengirim kuda buih yang membawanya ke dasar sungai dan ia tak pernah kembali.
claims.quote: Un giorno, per vendicare il figlio morto, un nobile inviò i suoi soldati a uccidere la fanciulla, soldati che seppero resistere al suo incanto e che l'avrebbero uccisa, se lei non avesse chiamato suo padre in aiuto: egli mandò un cavallo di schiuma che condusse la ninfa nelle profondità del fiume, da cui ella non fece più ritorno.

claims.statement: The figure often appears in German Romantic poetry, as in Heinrich Heine's Das Lied der Loreley (1827) or Joseph Freiherr von Eichendorff's Waldgespräch (1815); composer Alfredo Catalani drew on the myth for his opera Loreley.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh ini sering muncul dalam karya penyair Jerman era Romantik, seperti Das Lied der Loreley (1827) karya Heinrich Heine dan Waldgespräch (1815) karya Joseph Freiherr von Eichendorff; komponis Alfredo Catalani terinspirasi mitos ini untuk operanya Loreley.
claims.quote: Questa figura leggendaria si ritrova spesso nei componimenti dei poeti tedeschi dell'epoca romantica, come ad esempio in Das Lied der Loreley (1827) di Heinrich Heine o in Waldgespräch (1815) di Joseph Freiherr von Eichendorff. Fu inoltre proprio da questo mito che il compositore Alfredo Catalani trasse ispirazione per la sua opera Loreley.

claims.statement: Moss people (Moosleute), also wood folk (Holzleute) or forest folk (Waldleute), are a class of fairy-folk compared with dwarfs, elves or spirits, described in German folklore as intimately tied to trees and the forest.
claims.statement_id: Orang lumut (Moosleute), juga orang kayu (Holzleute) atau orang hutan (Waldleute), adalah golongan peri yang dibandingkan dengan kurcaci, elf, atau roh, digambarkan dalam cerita rakyat Jerman (German) memiliki ikatan erat dengan pohon dan hutan.
claims.quote: are a class of fairy-folk, variously compared to dwarfs, elves, or spirits, described in German folklore as having an intimate connection to trees and the forest.

claims.statement: In German, Schrat and Waldschrat also denote a moss person.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Jerman, kata Schrat dan Waldschrat juga dipakai untuk orang lumut.
claims.quote: In German, the words Schrat and Waldschrat are also used for a moss person.

claims.statement: Moss people are sometimes like dwarfs, child-sized but grey, old-looking, hairy and moss-clad; sometimes bigger, and in other accounts pretty.
claims.statement_id: Orang lumut kadang digambarkan mirip kurcaci, sebesar anak-anak, tetapi kelabu, tampak tua, berbulu, dan berbalut lumut; kadang lebih besar, dan dalam deskripsi lain cantik.
claims.quote: The moss people are sometimes described as similar to dwarfs, being the same size as children, but "grey and old-looking, hairy, and clad in moss." Sometimes, moss folk are also bigger. In other descriptions they are said to be pretty.

claims.statement: They resemble hamadryads: their lives are bound to the trees, and if someone rubs loose a tree's inner bark, a wood-woman dies.
claims.statement_id: Mereka mirip hamadryad: hidup mereka terikat pada pohon, dan bila seseorang membuat kulit dalam pohon terkelupas karena gesekan, seorang perempuan hutan mati.
claims.quote: They are similar to hamadryads. Their lives are "attached to the trees; if any one causes by friction the inner bark to loosen a Wood-woman dies."

claims.statement: Legend says these fairies sometimes borrowed things or asked for help but always repaid generously, often with advice or bread; they were easily angered if their gifts were spurned or if given caraway bread, crying 'Kümmelbrot, unser Tod!'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, peri-peri ini kadang meminjam barang atau minta bantuan tetapi selalu membalas dengan murah hati, sering dengan nasihat atau roti; mereka mudah marah bila hadiahnya ditolak atau diberi roti jintan, sambil berseru "Kümmelbrot, unser Tod!".
claims.quote: According to legend, these fairies would occasionally borrow items from people or ask for help but would always compensate the owners generously, often with either good advice or bread. It was, however, easy to anger such wood-sprites, either by spurning their gifts (which might be the compensations named above) or by giving them caraway bread

claims.statement: In some myths the moss folk ask people for breast milk for their young or steal human children, motifs of changeling lore.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian mitos, orang lumut meminta ASI kepada manusia untuk bayi mereka atau mencuri anak manusia, motif yang ada dalam cerita anak tukar (changeling).
claims.quote: In certain myths, the moss folk would ask humans for breast milk to feed their young, or steal little human children – motifs found in changeling lore.

claims.statement: Moss people, especially females, can send plagues yet also heal their victims; in epidemics the Holzfräulein came out of the forest to show which herbs cure or prevent plague.
claims.statement_id: Orang lumut, terutama yang perempuan, dapat mendatangkan wabah tetapi juga menyembuhkan korbannya; saat epidemi Holzfräulein keluar dari hutan untuk menunjukkan tanaman obat penyembuh atau penangkal wabah.
claims.quote: Moss people, especially the females of the species, are able to send plagues on one hand; on the other, they can also heal the victims of such plagues. During epidemics the Holzfräulein ("Wood ladies") would emerge from the forest to show the people which medicinal herbs could cure or ward off plague.

claims.statement: Moosweiblein appear in Sachsen, Thüringen, an der Saale, Orlagau, Harz, Vogtland, Oberpfalz, Bayerischen Wald, Franken, Oberfranken, Böhmerwald, around Warnsdorf in Nordtschechien, Riesengebirge and Westfalen (Saxony, Thuringia, Upper Palatinate, Bavarian Forest, Franconia, Giant Mountains, Westphalia).
claims.statement_id: Moosweiblein muncul di Sachsen, Thüringen, di tepi Saale, Orlagau, Harz, Vogtland, Oberpfalz, Bayerischen Wald, Franken, Oberfranken, Böhmerwald, sekitar Warnsdorf di Nordtschechien, Riesengebirge, dan Westfalen.
claims.quote: Moosweiblein treten in Sachsen, Thüringen, an der Saale, im Orlagau, im Harz, im Vogtland, in der Oberpfalz, im Bayerischen Wald, in Franken, in Oberfranken, im Böhmerwald, um Warnsdorf in Nordtschechien, im Riesengebirge und in Westfalen auf.

claims.statement: Moosweiblein live in the forest, on heaths, in dark places or the deepest woods; they dwell in earth holes, hollow trees, root huts or moss huts, sleep on moss and bed their children on moss or bark.
claims.statement_id: Moosweiblein tinggal di hutan, di padang, di tempat gelap, atau di hutan terdalam; rumahnya rongga tanah, pohon berlubang, pondok dari akar, atau pondok lumut; mereka tidur di atas lumut dan membaringkan anak-anaknya di atas lumut atau kulit kayu.
claims.quote: Die Moosweiblein leben im Wald. Sie wohnen auf der Heide, an dunklen Orten im Holz oder im tiefsten Wald. Ihre Behausung ist ein Erdloch, ein hohler Baum, ein Häuslein aus Baumwurzeln oder eine Mooshütte. Sie schlafen auf Moos und betten auch ihre Kinder auf Moos oder Rinde.

claims.statement: In Thuringia the only refuge for a Moosweibchen from the wild huntsman (the Wild Hunt; wilder Jäger) is a stump marked with three crosses by a woodsman while the tree was still falling.
claims.statement_id: Di Thüringen (Thuringia), satu-satunya tempat aman bagi Moosweibchen dari pemburu liar (Wild Hunt; wilder Jäger) adalah tunggul pohon yang ditandai tiga salib oleh penebang saat pohon itu masih tumbang.
claims.quote: In Thuringia, the only place where a Moosweibchen "little moss woman") is safe from the wild huntsman (German wilder Jäger) chasing her kind in the afternoon and at night is a tree stump marked with three crosses by a woodsman while the tree was still falling.

claims.statement: The female moss people, the Moosfräulein, have a queen called the Buschgroßmutter ('Shrub Grandmother').
claims.statement_id: Para perempuan lumut, Moosfräulein, memiliki ratu bernama Buschgroßmutter ("Nenek Semak").
claims.quote: The female Moss people, the Moosfräulein ("Moss ladies"), have a queen called the Buschgroßmutter (Buschgrossmutter; "Shrub Grandmother").

claims.statement: Selkolla ('seal-head') is a supernatural being of Icelandic folklore, a fair woman sometimes seen with a seal's head; she is chiefly attested as an antagonist of Bishop Guðmundur Arason (1161–1237), and her tales mix Christian ideas with Scandinavian non-Christian concepts.
claims.statement_id: Selkolla (harfiah "kepala anjing laut") adalah makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Islandia (Icelandic), perempuan cantik yang kadang terlihat berkepala anjing laut; ia terutama tercatat sebagai lawan Uskup Guðmundur Arason (1161–1237), dan kisahnya memadukan gagasan Kristen (Christian) dengan konsep tradisi Skandinavia (Scandinavian) non-Kristen.
claims.quote: Selkolla (literally 'seal-head') is a supernatural being in Icelandic folklore. She is described as a fair woman that is sometimes seen having the head of a seal. She is most prominently attested as an antagonist of Bishop Guðmundur Arason (1161–1237). Tales of Selkolla are noted for combining Christian ideas with concepts found in Scandinavian non-Christian traditions.

claims.statement: Then a woman is said to have newly arrived in the district, sometimes with an ordinary face, sometimes with a seal's head; this devil walked boldly by day and night, so this midday-devil was called Selkolla.
claims.statement_id: Lalu disebutkan seorang perempuan baru tiba di daerah itu, kadang berwajah biasa, kadang berkepala anjing laut; setan ini berkeliaran berani siang maupun malam, sehingga "setan tengah hari" ini disebut Selkolla.
claims.quote: It is then said that a certain woman is "newly arrived in the district, sometimes with an ordinary face but sometimes with a seal's head. This devil walked about as boldly by day as by night, for which reason this midday-devil was called Selkolla in the district".

claims.statement: The events of Selkollu þáttr take place in the Westfjords, beginning when a man and woman take a baby girl to be baptised.
claims.statement_id: Peristiwa Selkollu þáttr terjadi di Fjord Barat (Westfjords), bermula ketika seorang lelaki dan perempuan membawa bayi perempuan untuk dibaptis.
claims.quote: The events of Selkollu þáttr take place in the Westfjords, beginning when a man and woman are taking a baby girl to be baptised.

claims.statement: First, disguised as the farmer's wife, she tries to seduce him; when he realises and turns for home, Selkolla bars his way.
claims.statement_id: Mula-mula, menyamar sebagai istri petani, ia mencoba merayunya; ketika petani menyadarinya dan hendak pulang, Selkolla menghalangi jalannya.
claims.quote: First, in the guise of the farmer's wife, she tries to entice him into having sex. When he realises what is actually going on, he tries to turn for home, but Selkolla bars his way

claims.statement: Guðmundur (Guðmundr) knows her at once and drives her off with 'far niðr, fjandi, ok gakk ei framarr!' ('go down, devil, and don't come back!'); the next day he banishes her again by setting up seven crosses.
claims.statement_id: Guðmundur (Guðmundr) segera mengenalinya dan mengusirnya dengan kata "far niðr, fjandi, ok gakk ei framarr!" ("turunlah, setan, dan jangan kembali!"); keesokan harinya ia mengusirnya lagi dengan mendirikan tujuh salib.
claims.quote: Guðmundur realises immediately who it is and drives Selkolla away with the words "far niðr, fjandi, ok gakk ei framarr!" ("go down, devil, and don't come back!"). The next day, Guðmundr and Selkolla meet again and he drives her down once more, this time by setting up seven crosses.

claims.statement: The main medieval sources on Selkolla are versions B and D of Guðmundar saga Arasonar, the episode now often called Selkollu þáttr ('the Selkolla episode').
claims.statement_id: Sumber abad pertengahan utama kisah Selkolla adalah versi B dan D Guðmundar saga Arasonar, yang bagiannya kini sering disebut Selkollu þáttr ("episode Selkolla").
claims.quote: The main medieval source for stories about Selkolla is different versions of Guðmundar saga Arasonar, specifically versions B and D, where the episode is often now referred to as Selkollu þáttr ('the Selkolla episode').

claims.statement: Selkolla is a wondrous being of Icelandic (íslenskri) folk belief; a beautiful woman, sometimes seen with a seal's head.
claims.statement_id: Selkolla adalah makhluk ajaib dalam kepercayaan rakyat Islandia (íslenskri); ia perempuan cantik yang kadang terlihat berkepala anjing laut.
claims.quote: Selkolla er kynjavera í íslenskri þjóðtrú. Hún er falleg kona, en sést stundum með selshöfuð.

claims.statement: She is first mentioned in Sturla Þórðarson's Íslendinga saga, which says the bishop struggled with the being in the Westfjords (Vestfjörðum).
claims.statement_id: Selkolla pertama kali disebut dalam Íslendinga saga karya Sturla Þórðarson (Sturlu Þórðarson), yang menyatakan sang uskup bergulat dengan makhluk itu di Vestfirðir (Vestfjörðum).
claims.quote: Hennar er fyrst getið í Íslendinga sögu eftir Sturlu Þórðarson og er þar nefnt að biskupinn hafi glímt við veruna á Vestfjörðum.

claims.statement: The Selkolla story is thought to recall later folk tales of hidden-folk children and child ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Selkolla dianggap mengingatkan pada cerita rakyat yang lebih kemudian tentang anak-anak huldufólk dan hantu anak.
claims.quote: Sagan af Selkollu þykir minna á seinni tíma þjóðsögur af huldubörnum og barnadraugum.

claims.statement: Having finished, they go back to the child they had set down and find it 'black, dead, and hideous'; it later revives in a terrifying form and vanishes.
claims.statement_id: Selesai bersenggama, mereka kembali ke bayi yang mereka letakkan dan mendapatinya "hitam, mati, dan mengerikan"; bayi itu kemudian hidup lagi dengan rupa menakutkan lalu lenyap.
claims.quote: Once they have finished having sex, they return to the child, who they had set down, and find that it is now "black, dead, and hideous".

claims.statement: Only a diligent kinsman stays with him, until Selkolla overcomes him at night and bursts out his eyes; the farmer himself is left sick and robbed of his virility.
claims.statement_id: Hanya seorang kerabat yang rajin menemaninya, sampai Selkolla mengalahkannya di malam hari dan mencungkil matanya; petani itu sendiri jatuh sakit dan kehilangan kejantanan.
claims.quote: except for one diligent kinsman of his, who lies beside him until Selkolla overcomes him in the night and bursts out his eyes

claims.statement: On the way they take an 'immoral rest' beside a large stone aptly named Miklisteinn ('large stone').
claims.statement_id: Dalam perjalanan mereka melakukan "istirahat tak bermoral" di samping batu besar yang dinamai Miklisteinn ("batu besar").
claims.quote: On the way, they indulge in an "immoral rest" beside a large stone, fittingly called Miklisteinn ('large stone')

claims.statement: Eckart, commonly der treue Eckart or treuer Eckart ('the faithful Eckart'), is a figure of Germanic heroic legend, especially the Dietrich von Bern legends, and also features in German legends of the Wild Hunt.
claims.statement_id: Eckart, biasa disebut der treue Eckart atau treuer Eckart ("Eckart yang setia"), adalah tokoh legenda heroik Jermanik (Germanic), khususnya legenda Dietrich von Bern, dan juga muncul dalam legenda Jerman (German) tentang Perburuan Liar (wild hunt).
claims.quote: is a character of Germanic heroic legend, particularly the legends about Dietrich von Bern, and also features in German legends about the wild hunt.

claims.statement: In heroic legend Eckart (Eckehart, Eckewart) is the guardian of the Harlungs, two young men left the Breisgau, Breisach Castle and vast treasure by their late father Diether; he is a Harlung himself and renowned for loyalty; the Harlungs are cousins of Dietrich von Bern.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda heroik, Eckart (Eckehart, Eckewart) adalah wali para Harlung, dua pemuda yang mewarisi wilayah Breisgau, Kastel Breisach, dan harta tak terhingga dari mendiang ayah mereka Diether; ia sendiri Harlung dan termasyhur karena kesetiaannya; para Harlung adalah sepupu Dietrich von Bern.
claims.quote: In heroic legend, Eckart, also called Eckehart or Eckewart, is the guardian of the Harlungs, two young men whose late father Diether bequeathed them the Breisgau territory, Breisach Castle, and immeasurable treasure. He is a Harlung himself, and has great renown for his loyalty and faithfulness

claims.statement: In the Rabenschlacht Eckart captured Sibeche and dragged him on horseback to the gallows; he avenged his wards by killing Ermenrich with other heroes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pertempuran Rabenschlacht, Eckart menawan Sibeche dan menyeretnya dengan kuda ke tiang gantungan; ia membalas kematian anak-anak asuhnya dengan membunuh Ermenrich bersama pahlawan lain.
claims.quote: During the Rabenschlacht battle, Eckart took Sibeche captive and dragged him away on horseback to be hung on the gallows. He also took revenge for the demise of his charges when he and other heroes slew Ermenrich.

claims.statement: The Harlungs' treasure (Harlungenhort) is said to be enchanted in the Bürglenberg near Breisach, guarded by Eckart's spirit, who warns every treasure-seeker that it is fated for the true heir; hence the saying 'Du bist der treue Eckart, du warnest jedermann'.
claims.statement_id: Harta Harlung (Harlungenhort) konon disihir dan disembunyikan di gunung Bürglenberg dekat Breisach, dijaga arwah Eckart yang memperingatkan setiap pemburu harta bahwa harta itu ditakdirkan bagi ahli waris sejati; dari sini lahir pepatah "Du bist der treue Eckart, du warnest jedermann".
claims.quote: The rich treasure of the Harlungs, the Harlungenhort, is said to be enchanted and hidden inside the mountain Bürglenberg near Breisach. This treasure is guarded by the spirit of treuer Eckart who warns every treasure seeker that this treasure is fated to fall into the hands of the true heir of the Harlungs

claims.statement: In Thuringia Eckart is tied to the Wild Hunt (wütendes Heer) led by Frau Holle over the Twelve Nights of Christmas; he goes ahead of it, telling people to step aside so they come to no harm.
claims.statement_id: Di Thüringen (Thuringia), Eckart terkait dengan Perburuan Liar (wild hunt; wütendes Heer) yang dipimpin Frau Holle pada Dua Belas Malam Natal (Twelve Nights of Christmas); ia berjalan di depannya, menyuruh orang menyingkir agar tidak celaka.
claims.quote: In Thuringia, der treue Eckart is connected with the wild hunt, locally called wütendes Heer or furious host. Leader of the wild hunt is Frau Holle ... who roams the countryside with the furious host during Christmas, namely the Zwölften, that is the Twelve Nights of Christmas. Der treue Eckart goes ahead of the wild hunt, warning the people to step out of the way so they will suffer no harm.

claims.statement: He looks like an old man with a staff; when the host stays inside the Hörselberg, Eckart sits outside the cave warning all against entering the realm of Frau Venus (the Venusberg), whence none return.
claims.statement_id: Ia berwujud lelaki tua bertongkat; saat rombongan itu tinggal di dalam gunung Hörselberg, Eckart duduk di luar gua memperingatkan semua orang agar tidak memasuki alam Frau Venus (Venusberg), tempat tiada jalan kembali.
claims.quote: His appearance is that of an old man with a staff. When the furious host doesn’t travel and stays inside Hörselberg Mountain, der treue Eckart sits outside the cave, warning everybody against entering the realm of Frau Venus from where there is no return.

claims.statement: The Getreue Eckart or Treue Eckart is a figure rooted in Germanic legend and also a subject of literature and art.
claims.statement_id: Getreuer Eckart atau Treue Eckart adalah tokoh berakar dalam dunia legenda Jermanik dan juga bahan sastra serta seni.
claims.quote: Der Getreue Eckart oder Treue Eckart (auch in den diversen Namensvarianten von „Eckart“ wie „Eckhart“, „Eckehard“ usw.) ist eine Figur mit Wurzeln in der germanischen Sagenwelt, zugleich ein Stoff der Literatur und Kunst.

claims.statement: Eckart's guarding of the Venusberg entrance and warning people off is known since at least 1453; in Denmark he warns people before entering a brothel, and a chronicle of 1566 makes him a judge at the gates of hell.
claims.statement_id: Peran Eckart menjaga pintu Venusberg dan menasihati orang agar tidak masuk dikenal setidaknya sejak 1453; di Denmark ia memperingatkan orang sebelum memasuki rumah bordil, dan kronik tahun 1566 menempatkannya sebagai hakim di gerbang neraka.
claims.quote: That der treue Eckart guards the entrance to the Venusberg, i.e. the mountain of Frau Venus, and advises people against entering is known since 1453 if not longer, giving rise to the saying mentioned above. In Denmark, he also is found warning people before entering a brothel, and a chronicle from 1566 places him as a judge at the gates of hell.

claims.statement: Eckart refilled the children's beer jugs drunk by the Wild Hunt and promised they would stay full as long as the children kept silent about what they had seen (Thüringen).
claims.statement_id: Eckart mengisi kembali kendi bir anak-anak yang diminum rombongan Perburuan Liar dan berjanji kendi itu akan selalu penuh selama mereka merahasiakan apa yang mereka lihat (Thüringen).
claims.quote: Der Getreue Eckart macht sie ihnen wieder voll und verspricht, sie würden immer voll bleiben, solange die Kinder über das Geschaute Schweigen bewahrten.

claims.statement: Jörg Wickram used Eckart in the play Der trew Eckart (1532), and Johann Wolfgang Goethe made him the hero of the ballad Der getreue Eckart (1813).
claims.statement_id: Jörg Wickram memakai Eckart dalam lakon Der trew Eckart (1532), dan Johann Wolfgang Goethe menjadikannya tokoh utama balada Der getreue Eckart (1813).
claims.quote: Jörg Wickram använde Eckart i pjäsen Der trew Eckart från 1532. Johann Wolfgang Goethe gjorde honom till huvudperson i balladen Der getreue Eckart från 1813

claims.statement: One day while Eckart was away, King Ermenrich, the Harlungs' uncle, driven by greed for their inheritance and his adviser Sibeche's slanders, seized Breisach Castle, hanged his nephews and took their property.
claims.statement_id: Suatu hari saat Eckart tak ada, Raja Ermenrich, paman para Harlung, terdorong ketamakan akan warisan keponakannya dan fitnah penasihatnya Sibeche, merebut Kastel Breisach, menggantung keponakannya, dan merampas harta mereka.
claims.quote: One day, when Eckart was absent, King Ermenrich, uncle of the Harlungs, driven by both greed for his nephews’ heritage and his advisor Sibeche’s slanderous, fraudulent remarks

claims.statement: The Ulm Sparrow (Ulmer Spatz) is a landmark and symbol of the German city of Ulm, a bird statue atop Ulm Minster, the world's second-tallest church.
claims.statement_id: Burung Gereja Ulm (Ulmer Spatz) adalah tengara dan lambang kota Ulm di Jerman (German), berupa patung burung di atas Katedral Ulm (Ulm Minster), gereja tertinggi kedua di dunia.
claims.quote: The Ulm Sparrow (Ger. Ulmer Spatz) is a landmark in, and symbol of, the German city of Ulm. The landmark is a statue of a bird that sits atop the Ulm Minster, the second-tallest church in the world.

claims.statement: Legend says the people of Ulm carted a huge beam for building the minster (Münsters) but could not get it through the city gate; about to tear the gate down, they saw a sparrow carrying a twig for its nest.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, warga Ulm membawa balok sangat besar untuk membangun katedral (Münsters) tetapi tak bisa memasukkannya lewat gerbang kota; saat hendak merobohkan gerbang, mereka melihat burung gereja membawa ranting untuk sarangnya.
claims.quote: Der Sage nach sollen die Ulmer beim Bau des Münsters einen besonders großen Balken angekarrt haben. Sie schafften es aber nicht, ihn durch das Stadttor zu bringen. Als sie kurz davor waren, das Tor einzureißen, sahen sie einen Spatzen, der einen Zweig im Schnabel trug, um diesen in sein Nest einzubauen.

claims.statement: The sparrow turned the twig lengthwise before building it in; the Ulmers then saw the light and laid the beam lengthwise on their cart rather than across as before; the Ulmer Spatz is a landmark (Wahrzeichen) of Ulm.
claims.statement_id: Burung gereja itu memutar rantingnya memanjang sebelum menyusunnya; warga Ulm pun tersadar dan meletakkan balok memanjang di gerobak, bukan melintang seperti sebelumnya; Ulmer Spatz adalah lambang (Wahrzeichen) Ulm.
claims.quote: Dieser Spatz drehte den Zweig vor dem Einbau längsseits. Da ging dann wohl auch den Ulmern ein Licht auf und sie legten den Balken der Länge nach auf ihren Karren und nicht quer, wie bisher.

claims.statement: This humorous legend is traceable from the second quarter of the 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Legenda jenaka ini dapat dilacak sejak perempat kedua abad ke-19.
claims.quote: Diese humoristische Sage ist seit dem zweiten Viertel des 19. Jahrhunderts nachweisbar.

claims.statement: It belongs to a widespread cycle of tales about logs and beams carried crosswise, solved by watching a bird (sparrow, stork, jackdaw) build its nest; in 1872 Eduard Mauch called it a 'falsification of history' (Geschichtsfälschung).
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini termasuk kelompok kisah yang tersebar luas tentang batang kayu dan balok yang diangkut melintang, dipecahkan dengan mengamati burung (burung gereja, bangau, gagak) membangun sarang; pada 1872 Eduard Mauch menyebutnya "pemalsuan sejarah" (Geschichtsfälschung).
claims.quote: Sie gehört zu dem weit verbreiteten Sagenkreis um kreuzweis statt längsseits transportierte Baumstämme und Holzbalken, wobei die Lösung des Problems durch die Beobachtung eines Vogels (Sperling, Storch, Dohle etc.) beim Nestbau gewonnen wurde. Schon 1872 bezeichnete Eduard Mauch die Sage als eine „Geschichtsfälschung“

claims.statement: In 1842 Carl Hertzog published his poem 'Der Ulmer Spatz. Volkssage'.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1842 Carl Hertzog menerbitkan puisinya "Der Ulmer Spatz. Volkssage".
claims.quote: Bereits 1842 veröffentlichte Carl Hertzog (1810–nach 1874) sein Gedicht „Der Ulmer Spatz. Volkssage“.

claims.statement: The figure on the nave of Ulm Minster was donated by wealthy citizens; it is not a sparrow but a dove with an olive branch, as in the biblical story of Noah's Ark, and small relative to the building, easily seen only from the tower.
claims.statement_id: Sosok di atap nave Katedral Ulm (Ulm Minster) disumbangkan warga kaya; ia bukan burung gereja melainkan merpati pembawa ranting zaitun seperti kisah Bahtera Nuh (Noah's Ark), dan tampak kecil dibanding bangunannya, hanya mudah terlihat dari menara.
claims.quote: The figure on the nave of Ulm Minster was donated by wealthy citizens. It is not a sparrow, but a dove carrying an olive branch in its beak, as in the biblical story of Noah's Ark. It is small in relation to the building, and only easily visible from the tower.

claims.statement: The original Ulmer Spatz of 1858 from the minster roof (Münsterdach) is now in a display case near the entrance of Ulm Minster (Ulmer Münster).
claims.statement_id: Ulmer Spatz asli tahun 1858 dari atap katedral (Münsterdach) kini berada dalam lemari kaca di dekat pintu masuk Katedral Ulm (Ulmer Münster).
claims.quote: „Ulmer Spatz“: das Original aus dem Jahr 1858 vom Münsterdach befindet sich heute im Ulmer Münster nahe dem Eingang in einer Vitrine

claims.statement: The Wunderhirsch (wondrous stag) is a fabulous beast in the Hun and Hungarian (ungarischen) legend cycle.
claims.statement_id: Wunderhirsch (rusa ajaib) adalah hewan dongeng dalam siklus legenda Hun dan Hungaria (ungarischen).
claims.quote: Der Wunderhirsch ist ein Fabeltier im hunnischen und ungarischen Sagenkreis.

claims.statement: The legend survives in the Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum by medieval chronicler Simon Kézai; Hunor and Magor, sons of Ménrót and Eneth and ancestors of the Huns and Magyars, were led by the wondrous stag to a new land of settlement.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini terlestarikan dalam Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum karya penulis kronik abad pertengahan Simon Kézai; Hunor dan Magor, putra Ménrót dan Eneth, leluhur bangsa Hun dan Magyar, dituntun rusa ajaib ke wilayah permukiman baru.
claims.quote: Im Werk Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum des mittelalterlichen Chronisten Simon Kézai blieb die Sage erhalten. Die Söhne von Ménrót und Eneth, Hunor und Magor, von denen der Legende nach die Hunnen und Magyaren abstammen, wurden in der Sage vom Wunderhirsch in ein neues Siedlungsgebiet geführt.

claims.statement: Hunting on the steppe, they attacked a hind and chased it into the Meotis marshes, where it vanished from sight; they searched long in vain.
claims.statement_id: Saat berburu di stepa, mereka menyerang seekor rusa betina dan mengejarnya ke rawa-rawa Meotis, tempat hewan itu lenyap dari pandangan; mereka lama mencarinya tanpa hasil.
claims.quote: Als sie einmal zum Jagen weggingen, ereignete es sich, dass sie in einer Steppe eine Hirschkuh angriffen, der sie, wie sie vor ihnen herlief, in das Sumpfgebiet Meotis nachjagten. Und nachdem er dort vor ihren Augen völlig verschwand, suchten sie lange, doch gelang es ihnen nicht, sie zu finden.

claims.statement: The Hungarians (Ungarn) presumably brought this legend from eastern cultures at the time of the Landnahme; later it merged with the Christian legends of Eustace (Eustachius) and Hubert (Hubertus).
claims.statement_id: Diduga bangsa Hungaria (Ungarn) membawa legenda dari budaya timur ini saat penaklukan tanah air (Landnahme); kemudian legenda itu bercampur dengan legenda Kristen tentang Eustachius dan Hubertus.
claims.quote: Es ist zu vermuten, dass die Ungarn zur Zeit der Landnahme die aus östlichen Kulturen stammende Sage mit sich brachten. Später vermischte sie sich mit den christlichen Legenden von Eustachius und Hubertus.

claims.statement: It also appears in Hungarian neo-paganism and folklore as the csodaszarvas and is regarded as a national symbol.
claims.statement_id: Rusa ajaib juga muncul dalam neopaganisme Hungaria dan folklor sebagai csodaszarvas dan dianggap lambang nasional.
claims.quote: Er kommt auch im ungarischen Neuheidentum bzw. in der (ggf. völkisch missbrauchten) Folklore als csodaszarvas vor und gilt als nationales Symbol.

claims.statement: A csodaszarvas (wondrous stag) is a mitikus vezérállat, a mythical guiding animal sent by Isten (God), known in the hun-magyar mondakör (Hun-Hungarian legend cycle) and magyar népi hagyomány (Hungarian folk tradition).
claims.statement_id: A csodaszarvas (rusa ajaib) adalah mitikus vezérállat, hewan pemandu mitis kiriman Isten (Tuhan), dikenal dalam hun-magyar mondakör (siklus legenda Hun-Hungaria) dan magyar népi hagyomány (tradisi rakyat Hungaria).
claims.quote: A csodaszarvas a hun-magyar mondakörben és a magyar népi hagyományokban ismert, Isten által küldött mitikus vezérállat.

claims.statement: The csodaszarvas is a symbol of rebirth, renewal and the Sun (Nap).
claims.statement_id: Csodaszarvas adalah lambang kelahiran kembali, pembaruan, dan Matahari (Nap).
claims.quote: A csodaszarvas az újjászületés és a megújulás, valamint a Nap jelképe.

claims.statement: The wondrous stag also features as a path-showing animal in the anonymous Gesta Hungarorum, in the chapter on chieftain Bars (Bors) and the founding of his castle.
claims.statement_id: Rusa ajaib juga berperan sebagai hewan penunjuk jalan dalam Gesta Hungarorum anonim, pada bab tentang kepala suku Bars (Bors) dan pendirian bentengnya.
claims.quote: Der Wunderhirsch spielt auch in den anonymen Gesta Hungarorum im Kapitel über den Stammesführer Bars und der Gründung seiner Burg eine Rolle als den Weg weisendes Tier.

claims.statement: At last, at the edge of those marshes, they found land fit for keeping cattle.
claims.statement_id: Akhirnya, di tepi rawa-rawa itu mereka menemukan tanah yang cocok untuk beternak sapi.
claims.quote: Schließlich fanden sie am Eingang des erwähnten Sumpfgebietes für Rinderhaltung geeignetes Land vor.

claims.statement: Since ancient times the wondrous stag has been a sky sign for many Eurasian peoples and some North American tribes.
claims.statement_id: Sejak lama rusa ajaib menjadi lambang langit bagi banyak bangsa Eurasia (eurasischen) dan beberapa suku Amerika Utara (nordamerikanischen).
claims.quote: Der Wunderhirsch ist auch seit alten Zeiten ein Himmelszeichen bei vielen eurasischen Völkern und einigen nordamerikanischen Stämmen.

claims.statement: Research has shown parallels of this widespread motif group in East and West.
claims.statement_id: Penelitian telah menunjukkan kesejajaran kelompok motif yang tersebar luas ini di Timur dan Barat.
claims.quote: In der Forschung konnten Parallelen der weit verbreiteten Motivgruppe im Osten und Westen nachgewiesen werden.

claims.statement: Airón was a pre-Roman deity worshipped on the Iberian Peninsula and in parts of Gaul (Galliens).
claims.statement_id: Airón adalah dewa pra-Romawi yang dipuja di Semenanjung Iberia (Iberischen) dan sebagian Galia (Galliens).
claims.quote: Airón war eine prärömische Gottheit, die auf der Iberischen Halbinsel und in Teilen Galliens verehrt wurde.

claims.statement: Airón was connected with spring pools and wells and so revered as a god of life, yet also held to be a god of the underworld and death.
claims.statement_id: Airón terkait dengan mata air dan sumur sehingga dipuja sebagai dewa kehidupan, tetapi sekaligus dianggap dewa dunia bawah dan kematian.
claims.quote: Airón war verbunden mit Quelltöpfen und Brunnen und wurde insofern als Gott des Lebens verehrt. Gleichzeitig galt er aber auch als Gott der Unterwelt und des Todes.

claims.statement: Airón was a native god rooted in Hispania before the Roman (romanos) conquest; his cult was respected by the Romans, and he relates to deep waters in wells and lagoons and to chasms, hence a direct link with the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Airón adalah dewa pribumi Hispania sebelum penaklukan Romawi (romanos); kultusnya dihormati bangsa Romawi, dan ia terkait dengan perairan dalam di sumur dan laguna serta jurang, sehingga berhubungan langsung dengan dunia bawah.
claims.quote: Airón fue un dios indígena que estaba arraigado en Hispania antes de que los romanos emprendieran su conquista. Este dios, cuyo culto fue respetado por los romanos, se relaciona con aguas profundas (ubicadas en pozos y lagunas) y también con simas, por lo tanto hay una relación directa entre Airón y el inframundo.

claims.statement: In his positive aspect Airón is the god of life, as water and vegetation emerge from the underworld; in his negative aspect the god of death, as the underworld was where souls of the dead were thought to go.
claims.statement_id: Dalam aspek positifnya Airón dewa kehidupan, karena dari dunia bawah muncul air dan tumbuhan; dalam aspek negatifnya ia dewa kematian, karena dunia bawah dianggap tujuan jiwa orang mati.
claims.quote: En su aspecto positivo Airón es el dios de la vida, pues del inframundo emerge el agua (fuente de vida) y la vegetación. En su vertiente negativa, Airón se nos manifiesta como el dios de la muerte, pues el inframundo era el lugar a donde se consideraba —en las religiones precristianas— que iban a parar las almas de los muertos

claims.statement: No figurative images of the god are known; only springs and wells were revered.
claims.statement_id: Tidak diketahui ada gambaran figuratif dewa ini; yang dipuja hanyalah mata air dan sumur.
claims.quote: Figürliche Darstellungen des Gottes sind nicht bekannt; verehrt wurden lediglich Quellen und Brunnen.

claims.statement: Spain (España) has 101 Airón place names, plus six in France (Francia), eight in Portugal, and one each in Italy, Wales, Mexico and Brazil.
claims.statement_id: Di Spanyol (España) dikenal 101 nama tempat (topónimos) Airón seperti "Pozo Airón", ditambah enam di Prancis (Francia), delapan di Portugal, dan masing-masing satu di Italia, Wales, Meksiko, dan Brasil.
claims.quote: En España se conocen ciento un topónimos Airón, a los que se han de añadir seis hallados en Francia, ocho en Portugal, uno en Italia, uno en el País de Gales, uno en México y otro en Brasil.

claims.statement: At many sites with an Airón well there are horror legends whose protagonist dies by falling into the Airón well.
claims.statement_id: Di banyak tempat yang memiliki sumur Airón beredar legenda seram yang tokohnya tewas karena jatuh ke dalam sumur Airón.
claims.quote: aunque en muchos sitios donde existe un pozo Airón se encuentran leyendas de terror, en las que el protagonista termina muriendo al caer en el pozo Airón.

claims.statement: The inexhaustible well or unfathomable lagoon is really a metaphor for the channel joining the underworld, the world of the dead, with the earth of humans and the sky of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Sumur yang airnya tak habis atau laguna tak terduga dalamnya sebenarnya metafora saluran yang menghubungkan dunia bawah (dunia orang mati) dengan bumi tempat manusia dan langit tempat para dewa.
claims.quote: El pozo de agua inagotable o la laguna insondable en realidad son una metáfora que significa el canal que comunica el inframundo —o mundo de los muertos de donde no se puede salir— con la tierra habitada por los hombres y con el cielo donde se suponía que moraban los dioses.

claims.statement: In Norse mythology Árvakr (Old Norse 'early awake') and Alsviðr ('very quick') are the horses that pull the sun, or Sól's chariot, across the sky each day.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Árvakr (Nordik Kuno, "bangun pagi") dan Alsviðr ("sangat cepat") adalah kuda-kuda yang setiap hari menarik matahari, atau kereta Sól, melintasi langit.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Árvakr (Old Norse "early awake") and Alsviðr ("very quick") are the horses which pull the sun, or Sól's chariot, across the sky each day.

claims.statement: Both horses are named in Gylfaginning and Grímnismál, and their names often go with descriptions of the Sun.
claims.statement_id: Kedua kuda disebut dalam Gylfaginning dan Grímnismál, dan nama mereka sering dikaitkan dengan gambaran Matahari (Sun).
claims.quote: Both horses are mentioned in Gylfaginning and Grímnismál and their names are frequently associated with descriptions of the Sun.

claims.statement: Sól is abducted by the gods to drive the Sun in a chariot drawn by two horses; two large bellows (ísarnkol, 'cold iron') were set under the horses' shoulders against the Sun's immense heat.
claims.statement_id: Sól diculik para dewa untuk mengemudikan Matahari (Sun) dalam kereta yang ditarik dua kuda; dua puputan besar (ísarnkol, "besi dingin") dipasang di bawah bahu kedua kuda untuk melindunginya dari panas Matahari.
claims.quote: Sól is kidnapped by the gods to drive the Sun in a chariot pulled by two horses. Two large bellows (ísarnkol; cold iron) were placed under the shoulders of the two horses to protect them from the immense heat of the Sun.

claims.statement: Sól cannot stop driving, else Sköll will catch and devour the Sun; this is expected on the day of Ragnarök.
claims.statement_id: Sól tak bisa berhenti mengemudikan kereta, sebab Sköll akan menangkap dan menelan Matahari; hal itu diperkirakan terjadi pada hari Ragnarök.
claims.quote: Sól is unable to stop driving the chariot or else Sköll will catch the Sun and devour it; the Sun is expected to be caught and devoured on the day of Ragnarök.

claims.statement: The myth of Árvakr and Alsviðr is thought to have inspired English dramatist James Shirley's play The Triumph of Peace (1663).
claims.statement_id: Mitos Árvakr dan Alsviðr diduga mengilhami lakon The Triumph of Peace (1663) karya dramawan dan penyair Inggris (English) James Shirley.
claims.quote: The myth of Árvakr and Alsviðr is thought to have inspired English dramatist and poet James Shirley's play The Triumph of Peace (1663).

claims.statement: Årvången (Árvakr) in Norse (nordisk) mythology is one of the two horses pulling the sun across the sky.
claims.statement_id: Årvången (Árvakr) dalam mitologi Nordik (nordisk) adalah salah satu dari dua kuda yang menarik matahari melintasi langit.
claims.quote: Årvången er i nordisk mytologi en af de to heste der trækker solen over himlen (de har flere navne).

claims.statement: In Nordic mythology the gods govern days, nights and seasons and shape the Sun from a spark of Muspelheim's flame, but the Sun stands still without a driver.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, para dewa mengatur peredaran siang, malam, dan musim, serta membentuk Matahari dari percikan api Muspelheim, tetapi Matahari diam tanpa pengemudi.
claims.quote: In Nordic mythology, gods govern the passage of days, nights, and seasons, and shape the Sun from a spark of the flame Muspelheim, but the Sun stands still without a driver.

claims.statement: The horse-drawn Sun myth is not exclusive to Norse or Germanic religion; many other mythologies have a solar deity or Sun chariot drawn by horses.
claims.statement_id: Mitos Matahari yang ditarik kuda tidak khas agama Nordik atau Jermanik; banyak mitologi dan agama lain memiliki dewa matahari atau kereta Matahari yang ditarik kuda.
claims.quote: The myth of the Sun pulled by horses is not exclusive to Norse or Germanic religion. Many other mythologies and religions contain a solar deity or carriage of the Sun pulled by horses.

claims.statement: Ashaqlun (also Ashaqlūn) is a Manichaean demon (manichäischer Dämon) named in the Apocalypse of Adam (Apokalypse des Adam) in connection with the creation of Adam and Eve (Eva).
claims.statement_id: Ashaqlun (juga Ashaqlūn) adalah setan Manikheisme (manichäischer Dämon) yang disebut dalam Apokalipsis Adam (Apokalypse des Adam) dalam kaitannya dengan penciptaan Adam dan Hawa (Eva).
claims.quote: Ashaqlun, auch Ashaqlūn geschrieben, ist ein manichäischer Dämon, der in der Apokalypse des Adam im Zusammenhang mit der Erschaffung von Adam und Eva genannt wird.

claims.statement: Ashaqlun is the son of the King of Darkness (Königs der Finsternis); his consort is Namrael or Nebroel; they supposedly created the first human pair, Gehmurd (first man, Adam) and Murdiyanag (mother of life, Eve/Eva).
claims.statement_id: Ashaqlun adalah putra Raja Kegelapan (Königs der Finsternis); istrinya Namrael atau Nebroel; konon mereka menciptakan pasangan manusia pertama, Gehmurd (manusia pertama, Adam) dan Murdiyanag (ibu kehidupan, Hawa/Eva).
claims.quote: Ashaqlun ist der Sohn des Königs der Finsternis. Seine Gemahlin ist Namrael oder Nebroel. Angeblich erschufen sie das erste Menschenpaar, Gehmurd (Erster Mensch=Adam) und Murdiyanag (Mutter des Lebens=Eva).

claims.statement: Ashaqlun said: bring me your sons and daughters and give me some of the Light we have taken; it is I who will make for you a form like what you have seen, the first man.
claims.statement_id: Ashaqlun berkata: bawalah kepadaku putra-putri kalian dan berikan sebagian cahaya (Light) yang telah kita ambil; akulah yang akan membuatkan wujud seperti yang telah kalian lihat, yaitu manusia pertama (first man).
claims.quote: “Bring me your sons and daughters; come, give me some of the Light we have taken; it is I who will make for you a form like what you have seen, which is the first man (not the heavenly first man).”

claims.statement: They brought him their children; he ate the boys and gave the girls to his consort to feed on their 'life-lights' (Lebenslichtern); then the two united, Nebroel conceived and bore a son named Adam, and later a daughter named Eve (Eva).
claims.statement_id: Mereka membawa anak-anaknya kepadanya; ia memakan anak lelaki dan memberikan anak perempuan kepada istrinya untuk memakan "cahaya kehidupan" (Lebenslichtern) mereka; lalu keduanya bersatu, Nebroel hamil dan melahirkan putra bernama Adam, kemudian putri bernama Hawa (Eva).
claims.quote: Nun brachten sie ihre Kinder zu ihm und er verspeiste die Knaben und gab die Mädchen seiner Gemahlin, um sich an deren „Lebenslichtern“ zu nähren. Anschließend vereinigten sich die beiden und Nebroel wurde schwanger. Sie gebar einen Sohn, dem sie den Namen „Adam“ gab.

claims.statement: The aufhocker or huckup is a shapeshifter of German folklore.
claims.statement_id: Aufhocker atau huckup adalah makhluk pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Jerman (German).
claims.quote: The aufhocker ( German: [ˈaʊfˌhɔkɐ] ) or huckup ( German: [ˈhʊkˌʔʊp] ) is a shapeshifter in German folklore.

claims.statement: The Aufhocker is said to have no identifiable shape, taking forms such as a goblin, a beautiful woman, a dead man or various animals.
claims.statement_id: Aufhocker digambarkan tak punya bentuk yang dapat dikenali karena mengambil rupa goblin, perempuan cantik, orang mati, atau berbagai hewan.
claims.quote: The Aufhocker is described in German legend as having an unidentifiable shape because it takes on shapes such as a goblin, a beautiful woman, a dead man, or various animals.

claims.statement: The name Aufhocker means 'leap upon', since legend says it leaps onto victims' backs, often thieves and criminals needing a lesson, also lone travellers and old women.
claims.statement_id: Nama Aufhocker berarti "melompat ke atas", karena menurut legenda ia melompat ke punggung korbannya, sering pencuri dan penjahat yang perlu diberi pelajaran, juga pejalan sendirian dan perempuan tua.
claims.quote: The name Aufhocker means "leap upon". This name is used because according to legend, the Aufhocker would leap upon the back of its victims which are often thieves and criminals that need to be taught a lesson. Other common targets in the Aufhocker legend are lone travelers and old women.

claims.statement: Victims often die of exhaustion as the Aufhocker cannot be shaken off or killed, but travellers can free themselves by reaching home; attacks occur at bridges, crossroads, springs, woods, hollow paths and cemeteries.
claims.statement_id: Korban sering mati kelelahan karena Aufhocker tak bisa dienyahkan atau dibunuh, tetapi pejalan bisa bebas bila sempat sampai di rumah; serangan terjadi di jembatan, persimpangan, mata air, hutan, jalan cekung, dan pemakaman.
claims.quote: The victims often die of exhaustion because the Aufhocker cannot be shaken off or killed. However, it is believed that travelers can free themselves if they are able to make it home before being killed. These attacks often occur in specific locations such as bridges, crossroads, springs, woods, on a path through a hollow, and cemeteries.

claims.statement: Similar myths are found across most of Europe; in Charente-Maritime, France, the Ganipote is described with similar traits.
claims.statement_id: Mitos serupa ditemukan di sebagian besar Eropa (Europe); di Charente-Maritime, Prancis (France), Ganipote digambarkan bersifat serupa.
claims.quote: Similar myths can be found in most of Europe. In the Charente-Maritime département of France, the Ganipote is depicted as having similar traits.

claims.statement: The Aufhocker (Low German Huckup, Sorbian Bubak) is a kobold-like pressure spirit that leaps onto the shoulders or back of night travellers and grows heavier each step; it stays there until the traveller is freed by dawn light, a prayer or bells.
claims.statement_id: Aufhocker (Jerman Hilir Huckup, Sorbia Bubak) adalah roh penekan mirip kobold yang melompat ke bahu atau punggung pejalan malam dan makin berat di setiap langkah; ia tetap duduk di sana sampai pejalan dibebaskan oleh cahaya fajar, doa, atau dentang lonceng.
claims.quote: Der Aufhocker (niederdeutsch Huckup, sorbisch Bubak) ist in der Mythologie ein koboldartiger Druckgeist, der Wanderern, die nachts noch unterwegs sind, auf die Schultern oder den Rücken springt und mit jedem Schritt schwerer wird. ... Der Aufhocker bleibt auf dem Wanderer sitzen, bis dieser durch das heraufbrechende Licht, ein Gebet oder Glockenläuten von ihm erlöst wird

claims.statement: Aufhockers sometimes first appear as pitiable old women, but can also take animal forms such as a bear, calf (Bahkauv), werewolf (Stüpp) or dog.
claims.statement_id: Aufhocker kadang muncul sebagai perempuan tua yang memancing iba, tetapi juga bisa berwujud hewan seperti beruang, anak sapi (Bahkauv), manusia serigala (Stüpp), atau anjing.
claims.quote: Manchmal treten die Aufhocker zunächst als mitleiderregende alte Frauen in Erscheinung; sie können aber auch Tiergestalten wie Bär, Kalb (wie beim Bahkauv), Werwolf (wie beim Stüpp) oder Hund (wie beim Sürthgens Mossel) annehmen.

claims.statement: Typical haunted places such as brooks, bridges, lakes, woods, ditches, crossroads, sunken lanes, churchyards and murder or execution sites are where one usually meets the Aufhocker.
claims.statement_id: Tempat angker yang khas seperti sungai kecil, jembatan, danau, hutan, parit, persimpangan, jalan cekung, pemakaman, serta tempat pembunuhan atau eksekusi adalah lokasi umum pertemuan dengan Aufhocker.
claims.quote: Typische Spukorte wie Bäche, Brücken, Seen, Wälder, Gräben, Wegkreuzungen, Hohlwege, Kirchhöfe und Mord- oder Richtstätten sind die übliche Stelle für eine Begegnung mit dem Aufhocker

claims.statement: Belief in the Aufhocker stems from fear of the Wiedergänger (revenant); the oldest reports clearly speak of 'corpses leaping onto backs' (aufhuckenden Leichen), not kobolds or ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan akan Aufhocker berakar pada ketakutan terhadap Wiedergänger (mayat hidup); laporan tertua jelas berbicara tentang "mayat yang melompat ke punggung" (aufhuckenden Leichen), bukan kobold atau hantu.
claims.quote: Seine Ursprünge hat der Glaube an den Aufhocker jedoch in der Furcht vor dem Wiedergänger, dem Untoten. Die ältesten Berichte über Aufhocker sprechen eindeutig von „aufhuckenden Leichen“ und nicht von Kobolden oder Gespenstern.

claims.statement: The Aufhocker is sometimes said to tear out human throats rather than exhaust its victims; this version is linked to vampirism.
claims.statement_id: Aufhocker kadang dikatakan merobek leher manusia alih-alih membunuh korban dengan kelelahan; versi ini dikaitkan dengan vampirisme.
claims.quote: The Aufhocker is a very dangerous theriomorph that is sometimes said to tear out the throats of humans instead of killing its victims from exhaustion. The version of the Aufhocker that attacks victims' throats is linked to vampirism.

claims.statement: The Hackestüpp of Düren is such an Aufhocker: it first follows victims as a playful puppy, then leaps onto their backs, cannot be shaken off and grows heavier step by step.
claims.statement_id: Hackestüpp dari Düren juga Aufhocker: mula-mula menemani korbannya sebagai anak anjing yang lucu, lalu melompat ke punggung mereka, tak bisa dienyahkan, dan makin berat di setiap langkah.
claims.quote: Um solch einen Aufhocker handelt es sich auch bei dem Hackestüpp von Düren, der seine Opfer zunächst als verspieltes Hündchen begleitet, ihnen dann auf den Rücken springt, sich nicht mehr abschütteln lässt und von Schritt zu Schritt schwerer wird.

claims.statement: The Bahkauv ('brook calf') is an Aachen legend figure said to frighten drunken men at night and demand to be carried on their shoulders.
claims.statement_id: Bahkauv ("anak sapi sungai") adalah tokoh legenda Aachen (Aachener) yang konon menakuti lelaki mabuk pada malam hari dan meminta digendong di bahu mereka.
claims.quote: Das Bahkauv („Bachkalb“) ist eine Aachener Sagengestalt, die nachts betrunkene Männer erschrecken und sie auffordern soll, sie auf ihren Schultern zu tragen.

claims.statement: The traveller is as if paralysed, feels oppressed and cannot turn around.
claims.statement_id: Pejalan seperti lumpuh, merasa sesak, dan tak mampu menoleh.
claims.quote: Der Wanderer ist wie gelähmt, leidet unter Beklemmung und ist unfähig sich umzuwenden.

claims.statement: The Bergmönch ('mountain monk') is a mountain spirit of German folklore, also called Meister Hämmerling.
claims.statement_id: Bergmönch ("biarawan gunung") adalah roh gunung dari cerita rakyat Jerman (German), juga dikenal sebagai Meister Hämmerling.
claims.quote: The Bergmönch ("mountain monk"; German: [ˈbɛʁkˌmœnç] ) is a mountain spirit from German folklore. He is also known as Meister Hämmerling ("master hammering guy").

claims.statement: The Bergmönch is white-haired, with fiery plate-sized eyes and a black monk's hooded cowl; he can dress as a miner (Meister Hämmerling), become a long-necked horse and turn invisible.
claims.statement_id: Bergmönch berambut putih, bermata menyala sebesar piring, berjubah bertudung hitam seperti biarawan; ia bisa berpakaian penambang (Meister Hämmerling), menjelma kuda berleher panjang, dan menjadi tak terlihat.
claims.quote: He has white hair and fiery looking eyes as large as dining plates. The mountain spirit wears a black hooded cowl as used by monks; this gave rise to his name Bergmönch. He also can be dressed like a miner. As such he is called Meister Hämmerling. Additionally, he can take the shape of a horse with long neck and terrible looking eyes, and is also able to become invisible.

claims.statement: The Bergmönch dwells in mountain pits and mines, active deep down and at the surface, busiest on Fridays, moving ore from one bucket to another.
claims.statement_id: Bergmönch tinggal di lubang dan tambang di pegunungan, aktif di kedalaman maupun permukaan, terutama sibuk pada hari Jumat (Fridays) memindahkan bijih dari satu ember ke ember lain.
claims.quote: The residence of the Bergmönch are pits and mines in the mountains. There he is active as well deep in the pits as up on the surface. Especially on Fridays this mountain spirit is very busy. He fills the excavated ores from one bucket to another.

claims.statement: The mountain spirit is generally an erratic, dangerous being; his poisonous breath can kill twelve people at once.
claims.statement_id: Roh gunung ini umumnya makhluk yang tak menentu dan berbahaya; napasnya beracun dan dapat membunuh dua belas orang sekaligus.
claims.quote: The mountain spirit generally is an erratic and dangerous being. His breath is poisonous, able to kill twelve people at once.

claims.statement: The Bergmönch can also be just and helpful, guarding good miners and punishing evil ones; he punishes whistling, cursing, egoism, infidelity and idleness, once killing an evil foreman by invisibly crushing his head.
claims.statement_id: Bergmönch juga bisa adil dan menolong, melindungi penambang baik dan menghukum yang jahat; ia menghukum kebiasaan bersiul, mengumpat, egois, tidak setia, dan malas, misalnya membunuh mandor jahat dengan meremukkan kepalanya secara tak terlihat.
claims.quote: The Bergmönch can also be just and helpful, guarding the good miners and punishing the evil ones. He punishes vices such as whistling and cursing, egoism, infidelity and idleness. For example, the mountain spirit killed an evil foreman of miners by crushing his head invisibly with his knees.

claims.statement: The oil he gives never diminishes and burns for years so long as the miner keeps the secret; he also does the work of favourite miners, digging ore for them.
claims.statement_id: Minyak lampu pemberiannya tak pernah berkurang dan menyala bertahun-tahun selama penambang tak membuka rahasianya; ia juga mengerjakan pekerjaan penambang kesayangannya, menggali bijih bagi mereka.
claims.quote: This oil never diminishes and burns steadily even for years when the miner never reveals the secret that he got lamp oil from the Bergmönch. He also has favorite miners whose work he does, excavating ores for them.

claims.statement: The Bergmönch became a highly contradictory figure: besides a monk he appears as a hooded giant with sparkling eyes as big as coach wheels, as a foreman or mine master (Bergmeister) with a silver lamp, or as a mine juror.
claims.statement_id: Bergmönch menjadi tokoh yang sangat kontradiktif: selain sebagai biarawan, ia tampil sebagai raksasa bertudung dengan mata berkilat sebesar roda kereta, sebagai mandor atau kepala tambang (Bergmeister) dengan lampu tambang perak, atau sebagai pengawas tambang.
claims.quote: Besonders der Bergmönch wurde zu einer ausgesprochen widersprüchlichen Figur: anstatt in der Gestalt eines Mönches erscheint er auch als Riese mit Kapuze (mit sprühenden Augen, groß wie Kutschenräder), in der Gestalt eines Steigers oder Bergmeisters (mit einem silbernen Grubenlicht) oder noch häufiger als Geschworener.

claims.statement: Some legends hold him to be the ghost of a dead mine master (Bergmeister) unable to leave his beloved work, now haunting the galleries forever; still dangerous, he kills complaining miners with his poisonous breath.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian legenda ia dianggap hantu kepala tambang (Bergmeister) yang tak bisa berpisah dari pekerjaannya dan kini selamanya bergentayangan di terowongan; ia tetap berbahaya, membunuh dengan napas beracun penambang yang mengeluhkannya.
claims.quote: Tatsächlich wird er in manchen Sagen für das Gespenst eines toten Bergmeisters gehalten, der sich nicht von seiner geliebten Arbeit trennen konnte, und nun für immer in den Stollen und Gruben umgehen muss. Noch immer ist er gefährlich, wie ein Bergteufel, und tötet mit seinem Gifthauch die Bergleute, die sich über ihn beschweren.

claims.statement: He shows favourite miners hidden lodes of gold and silver, but the miner must throw some tools into the lode or it closes, never to be seen again.
claims.statement_id: Ia menunjukkan urat emas dan perak tersembunyi kepada penambang kesayangannya, tetapi penambang harus melempar sebagian alatnya ke urat itu, atau urat itu akan tertutup selamanya.
claims.quote: He also shows his favourite miners hidden lodes of gold and silver but the miner has to throw some of his mining tools in the offered lode or it will be closed to never being seen by human eyes again.

claims.statement: He makes galleries collapse or causes inrushes of water and firedamp.
claims.statement_id: Ia meruntuhkan terowongan atau menimbulkan banjir dan ledakan gas tambang.
claims.quote: Er lässt Stollen einstürzen oder verursacht Wassereinbrüche und Schlagwetter.

claims.statement: The Bergmönch is giant-like in size.
claims.statement_id: Bergmönch berukuran seperti raksasa.
claims.quote: The appearance of the Bergmönch is like a giant in size.

claims.statement: The Bergsrå (Mountain Rå), Bergatrollet (Mountain Troll) or Bergakungen (Mountain King) was a mythical creature or mountain spirit in Norse mythology.
claims.statement_id: Bergsrå (Rå Gunung), Bergatrollet (Troll Gunung), atau Bergakungen (Raja Gunung) adalah makhluk mitis atau roh gunung dalam mitologi Nordik (Norse).
claims.quote: The Bergsrå (Mountain Rå), Bergatrollet (Mountain Troll), or Bergakungen (Mountain King) was a mythical creature or spirit of the mountain in Norse mythology.

claims.statement: The bergsrå could be male or female, living in the mountain with a court of relatives and sometimes trolls; it commonly tricked people into its mountain home so they became bergtagen ('taken into the mountain').
claims.statement_id: Bergsrå bisa laki-laki atau perempuan, tinggal di gunung bersama istana kerabat dan kadang dikelilingi troll; ia lazim memperdaya orang masuk ke kediamannya di gunung sehingga mereka menjadi bergtagen ("diambil ke dalam gunung").
claims.quote: The bergsrå could be either masculine or feminine. It lived in the mountain with a court of relatives and sometimes surrounded by trolls. It was a common phenomenon in the mythology about the bergsrå to trick people into their dwellings in the mountain and to become bergtagen

claims.statement: A typical account was given by Sven Andersson in 1691 when tried for intercourse with a female bergsrå.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran khas kejadian semacam itu diberikan Sven Andersson pada 1691 ketika ia diadili karena bersetubuh dengan bergsrå perempuan.
claims.quote: A typical description of such a claimed occurrence was given by Sven Andersson in 1691 when he was on trial for having sexual intercourse with a female bergsrå.

claims.statement: Bergsrået (bergatrollet, bergakungen) in Nordic (nordisk) folk belief is a supernatural being living in the mountain and ruling its ore; it often twists the sight of those who find ore deposits so they cannot find them again, and in many tales is surrounded by family and a court of trolls.
claims.statement_id: Bergsrået (bergatrollet, bergakungen) dalam kepercayaan rakyat Nordik (nordisk) adalah makhluk gaib yang tinggal di gunung dan menguasai bijihnya; ia sering mengacaukan penglihatan orang yang menemukan endapan bijih sehingga tak bisa menemukannya lagi, dan dalam banyak cerita dikelilingi keluarga dan istana troll.
claims.quote: Bergsrået, eller bergatrollet eller bergakungen, var i nordisk folktro ett övernaturligt väsen, som bor i berget och råder över dess malm. Bergsrået förvänder ofta synen på dem som råkat upptäcka malmfyndigheter, så att de senare inte kan hitta dem. I många berättelser omges bergsrået av sin familj och ett hov av troll.

claims.statement: Dealings between humans and a bergrå were long seen as real; one who had them was taken into the mountain, called bergtagning, a known phenomenon in bergsrå lore.
claims.statement_id: Hubungan antara manusia dan bergrå lama dianggap nyata; orang yang melakukannya diambil ke dalam gunung, disebut bergtagning, fenomena terkenal dalam mitologi bergsrå.
claims.quote: Umgänge mellan människor och bergrå var något som långt fram i tiden sågs som en realitet: en människa som hade gjort detta blev tagen in i berget, något som kallades bergtagning och var ett känt fenomen inom mytologin kring bergsrået.

claims.statement: In 1691 farmhand Sven Andersson of Vättle hundred in Västergötland was sentenced to death for intercourse with a female bergrå.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1691 buruh tani Sven Andersson dari Vättle, Västergötland, dijatuhi hukuman mati karena bersetubuh dengan bergrå perempuan.
claims.quote: År 1691 dömdes en dräng, Sven Andersson från Vättle härad i Västergötland, till döden för att ha haft samlag med ett kvinnligt bergrå .

claims.statement: The farmhand said he had once fallen asleep in the forest by a mountain while seeking a stray goat and was taken into the mountain by a woman in white, who gave him food and drink and then lay with him.
claims.statement_id: Buruh tani itu mengaku pernah tertidur di hutan dekat gunung saat mencari kambing yang lepas, lalu dibawa ke dalam gunung oleh perempuan berbaju putih yang memberinya makan dan minum, lalu bersetubuh dengannya.
claims.quote: Drängen hade förklarat att han en gång somnat i skogen vid ett berg då han letat efter en bortsprungen get och då tagits in i berget av en kvinna i vitt. Kvinnan hade gett honom mat och dryck och sedan haft samlag med honom.

claims.statement: Blainn (Old Norse Bláinn) is a term in Norse (nordischen) poetry also used for mythical beings.
claims.statement_id: Blainn (Nordik Kuno: Bláinn) adalah istilah dalam puisi Nordik (nordischen) yang juga dipakai untuk makhluk mitis.
claims.quote: Blainn (altnordisch Bláinn) ist in der nordischen Dichtung ein Begriff, der auch für mythische Wesen verwendet wurde.

claims.statement: It was used as a byname both for the primeval giant Ymir and for dwarfs, and also for non-mythical things such as a part of the sky.
claims.statement_id: Istilah ini dipakai sebagai sebutan bagi raksasa purba Ymir maupun kurcaci, dan juga untuk hal nonmitis seperti bagian langit.
claims.quote: Er wurde sowohl als Umschreibung für den Vorzeitriesen Ymir als auch für Zwerge gebraucht. Das Wort konnte aber auch zur Umschreibung von nichtmythischen Dingen verwendet werden, wie zum Beispiel einem Teil des Himmels.

claims.statement: Bláinn is held to derive from Old Norse blár 'blue, dark, black', so the names are rendered 'the dark-coloured one', 'blue corpse' or 'the bluing one'.
claims.statement_id: Bláinn dianggap turunan dari Nordik Kuno blár, "biru, gelap, hitam", sehingga diterjemahkan "yang berwarna gelap", "mayat biru", atau "yang membiru".
claims.quote: Bláinn gilt als Ableitung von altnordisch blár „blau, dunkel, schwarz“. Man übersetzt somit die mythischen Namen als „der Dunkel-Farbige“, „Blau-Leiche“ oder „der Blauende.“

claims.statement: Völuspá 9: the gods strode to their judgement seats and deliberated who should create the race of dwarfs from Brimir's blood and Blainn's bones; in Eddic poetry the term occurs only in Völuspá.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Völuspá 9: para dewa melangkah ke kursi pengadilan dan bermusyawarah siapa yang akan menciptakan bangsa kurcaci dari darah Brimir dan tulang Blainn; istilah ini dalam puisi Edda hanya muncul di Völuspá.
claims.quote: „Da schritten alle Rater zum Richterstuhl, die heiligsten Götter, und beratschlagten, wer das Volk der Zwerge erschaffen sollte aus Brimirs Blut und aus Blainns Knochen.“

claims.statement: The phrase 'from Brimir's blood and Blainn's bones' seems to allude to the gods making the sea and mountains from Ymir's blood and bones, as Grimnismál and Vafþrúðnismál relate.
claims.statement_id: Ungkapan "dari darah Brimir dan tulang Blainn" tampaknya merujuk penciptaan laut dan gunung dari darah dan tulang Ymir oleh para dewa, seperti dikisahkan Grimnismál dan Vafþrúðnismál.
claims.quote: Die Wendung „aus Brimirs Blut und Blainns Knochen“ scheint darauf anzuspielen, dass die Götter das Meer und die Berge aus Ymirs Blut und Knochen schufen, wie zwei andere Lieder der Lieder-Edda überliefern, das Grimnismál und das Vafþrúðnismál.

claims.statement: It is surmised that Bláinn could denote the giant because, per both poems, the sky, and thus its blue, was made from his skull.
claims.statement_id: Diduga Bláinn bisa dipakai sebagai sebutan bagi sang raksasa karena menurut kedua puisi itu langit, beserta warna birunya, diciptakan dari tengkoraknya.
claims.quote: Man mutmaßt, dass Bláinn als Umschreibung für den Riesen gebraucht werden konnte, weil nach den beiden Liedern der Himmel aus seinem Schädel erschaffen wurde – und damit auch das Blau des Himmels.

claims.statement: In the Þulur Bláinn is listed as a heiti for dwarf; a poet could use Bláinn as another word for dwarf.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Þulur, Bláinn tercantum sebagai heiti untuk kurcaci; artinya penyair bisa memakai Bláinn sebagai kata lain untuk kurcaci.
claims.quote: In den Þulur wird Bláinn als Heiti für Zwerg angeführt. Das heißt, ein Dichter konnte Bláinn als alternatives Wort für Zwerg verwenden.

claims.statement: The English article says Ymir in Norse mythology, also called Aurgelmir, Brimir or Bláinn, is the ancestor of all jötnar.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Inggris menyebut Ymir dalam mitologi Nordik (Norse), yang juga disebut Aurgelmir, Brimir, atau Bláinn, sebagai leluhur semua jötnar.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Ymir (/ˈiːmɪər/), also called Aurgelmir, Brimir, or Bláinn, is the ancestor of all jötnar.
