claims.statement: In Norse mythology a Brunnmigi (Old Norse 'pees in a well') is a being that defiles wells met by King Hjörleifr in Hálfs saga ok Hálfsrekka and, per the Prose Edda þulur, also a kenning for foxes; it is a large beast.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Brunnmigi (Nordik Kuno, "kencing di sumur") adalah makhluk yang mencemari sumur yang ditemui Raja Hjörleifr dalam Hálfs saga ok Hálfsrekka dan, menurut þulur Edda Prosa (Prose Edda), juga kenning untuk rubah; ia makhluk besar.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, a Brunnmigi (Old Norse "pees in a well") is a being who defiles wells encountered by King Hjörleifr in Hálfs saga ok Hálfsrekka and, as recorded in the Prose Edda þulur, is also a kenning applied to foxes. It is a large beast.

claims.statement: The Spanish article likewise calls the Brunnmigi a being of Norse (nórdica) mythology that defiles wells met by King Hjörleifr in Hálfs saga ok Hálfsrekka.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Spanyol juga menyebut Brunnmigi makhluk dalam mitologi Nordik (nórdica) yang mencemari sumur yang ditemui Raja Hjörleifr dalam Hálfs saga ok Hálfsrekka.
claims.quote: En la mitología nórdica, un Brunnmigi (nórdico antiguo "hace pis en un pozo") es un ser que profana los pozos encontrados por el rey Hjörleifr en Hálfs saga ok Hálfsrekka

claims.statement: The Brunnmigi appears in the second book of the Magnus Chase and the Gods of Asgard series, The Hammer of Thor (El Martillo de Thor).
claims.statement_id: Brunnmigi disebut dalam buku kedua seri Magnus Chase dan Para Dewa Asgard (Magnus Chase y los dioses de Asgard), The Hammer of Thor (El Martillo de Thor).
claims.quote: El Brunnmigi es mencionado en el segundo libro de la serie "Magnus Chase y los dioses de Asgard", El Martillo de Thor

claims.statement: The Buschgroßmutter ('shrub grandmother') is a legendary creature of German folklore, especially in Thuringia, Saxony, Silesia and Bohemia, called Pusch-Grohla and Buschmutter in Silesia and Buschweibchen in Bohemia.
claims.statement_id: Buschgroßmutter ("nenek semak") adalah makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Jerman (German), terutama di Thüringen (Thuringia), Sachsen (Saxony), Silesia, dan Bohemia, dengan nama daerah Pusch-Grohla dan Buschmutter di Silesia serta Buschweibchen di Bohemia.
claims.quote: is a legendary creature from German folklore, especially found in folktales from the regions Thuringia, Saxony, former German-speaking Silesia and the former German-speaking parts of Bohemia. She is called various regional names such as Pusch-Grohla ("shrub granny" in Silesian German) and Buschmutter ("shrub mother") in Silesia, 's Buschkathel ("th' Shrub-Katie") and Buschweibchen in Bohemia

claims.statement: The Buschgroßmutter is a forest spirit of the deepest woods, showing herself only once a century; ancient, small, stooped, wrinkled and staring, with long snow-white but tangled, lice-ridden hair.
claims.statement_id: Buschgroßmutter adalah roh hutan di hutan terdalam yang menampakkan diri hanya sekali tiap seratus tahun; ia sangat tua, kecil, bungkuk, keriput, bermata melotot, berambut panjang seputih salju tetapi kusut dan berkutu.
claims.quote: The Buschgroßmutter is a forest spirit living in the deepest woods which shows herself to humans only once every hundred years. She is as old as the hills, her appearance being small and ducked, wrinkly and ugly. She has staring eyes and is sometimes said to have an iron head, a typical demonic feature. The Buschgroßmutter's hair is long, as white as snow, but messy and full of lice.

claims.statement: When the mountains 'smoke' with fog in spring and autumn, the Buschweibchen is said to be cooking.
claims.statement_id: Bila pegunungan "berasap" oleh kabut pada musim semi dan gugur, Buschweibchen dikatakan sedang memasak.
claims.quote: When the mountains are "smoking" with fog in spring and autumn, then the Buschweibchen is said to be cooking.

claims.statement: The Buschgroßmutter's character wavers between benevolent and malevolent; she asks people to comb or delouse her hair, and those who comply get an endless clew of yarn or green or yellow leaves that later become gold if kept.
claims.statement_id: Watak Buschgroßmutter mendua antara baik dan jahat; ia meminta orang menyisir atau mencari kutu di rambutnya, dan yang memenuhinya diberi gulungan benang tak habis atau daun hijau atau kuning yang kelak menjadi emas bila tak dibuang.
claims.quote: The character of the Buschgroßmutter is ambivalent, fluctuating between benevolent and malevolent behaviour. She asks people to comb or louse her hair. Those who fulfill her request will be rewarded with a neverending clew of yarn ... or with either green or yellow leaves which will later become gold if not thrown away.

claims.statement: Tidying her hair is very hard since her head is ice-cold, briefly freezing the helper's hands; when sneered at, the Buschgroßmutter takes revenge by breathing on the mocker, who falls ill, usually with a rash.
claims.statement_id: Merapikan rambutnya sangat sulit karena kepalanya sedingin es sehingga tangan penolong membeku sementara; bila diejek, Buschgroßmutter membalas dengan menghembuskan napas pada pengejek, yang lalu sakit, biasanya ruam kulit.
claims.quote: It is but very difficult to clean and tidy the Buschweibchen's hair because her head is as cold as ice, thus leading to a (temporary) freezing of the helper's hands. When she was sneered at, the Buschgroßmutter takes revenge by breathing on the sneerer which will result in illnesses, most commonly rash.

claims.statement: The Buschgroßmutter is usually solitary, but at times said to lead a band of Moosfräulein, female forest spirits called her daughters, roaming the land with them in the holy nights.
claims.statement_id: Biasanya Buschgroßmutter penyendiri, tetapi kadang dikatakan memimpin rombongan Moosfräulein, roh hutan perempuan yang disebut putri-putrinya, dan bersama mereka berkeliling negeri pada malam-malam suci.
claims.quote: Normally the Buschgroßmutter is a solitary figure, but occasionally she is said to be the leader of a horde of Moosfräulein ("moss ladies"), female forest spirits which are said to be her daughters. Accompanied by her daughters, the Buschgroßmutter roams the countryside in holy nights.

claims.statement: By the Saale the Buschgroßmutter is called mistress of the Moosweiblein; strictly she is their mother (Moosfräuleins), roaming the land with them, usually in a little cart; with tangled hair and a fixed stare, she is also a bogey for children and corresponds to Frau Holle or Perchta.
claims.statement_id: Di tepi Saale, Buschgroßmutter disebut nyonya para Moosweiblein; tepatnya ia ibu para Moosweiblein (Moosfräuleins) yang berkeliling negeri bersamanya dengan kereta kecil; rambutnya kusut, tatapannya kaku, ia juga penakut anak, dan sepadan dengan Frau Holle atau Perchta.
claims.quote: Als Herrin der Moosweiblein wird an der Saale die Buschgroßmutter bezeichnet. Die Buschgroßmutter ist genau genommen die Mutter der Moosweiblein (hier: Moosfräuleins), mit welchen sie im Lande umherzieht, meist in einem kleinen Rollwagen. Sie hat wirres Haar und einen starren Blick. Die Buschgroßmutter ist auch ein Kinderschreck. Sie entspricht der andernorts verbreiteten Frau Holle oder Perchta.

claims.statement: In the 19th century mythologists like Jacob Grimm and Wilhelm Mannhardt made the Buschgroßmutter leader or even queen of the moss people, like an elf queen.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-19 para mitolog seperti Jacob Grimm dan Wilhelm Mannhardt menyatakan Buschgroßmutter pemimpin atau bahkan ratu orang lumut, seperti ratu elf.
claims.quote: In the 19th century, mythologists such as Jacob Grimm or Wilhelm Mannhardt declared the Buschgroßmutter to be the leader or even the queen of the moss people, similar to the elf queen.

claims.statement: In folktales of the German-speaking Transylvanian Saxons, in today's Romania, there is a similar being called Baschgrîs, Baschmôter or Baschäinjel.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Saxon Transilvania (Transylvanian Saxons) berbahasa Jerman di Transilvania, kini bagian Rumania, terdapat makhluk serupa bernama Baschgrîs, Baschmôter, atau Baschäinjel.
claims.quote: In traditional folktales of the German-speaking Transylvanian Saxons in Transylvania, today part of Romania, there is a similar being called Baschgrîs ("shrub grandmother"), Baschmôter ("shrub mother") or Baschäinjel ("shrub angel") in Transylvanian Saxon dialect.

claims.statement: Though 19th-century mythologists regarded her as queen of the moss people (Moosleute), she is rather seen as a primitive forest demon.
claims.statement_id: Meski para mitolog abad ke-19 menganggapnya ratu orang lumut (Moosleute), ia lebih dipandang sebagai setan hutan primitif.
claims.quote: Während sie von den Mythologen des 19. Jahrhunderts als Königin der Moosleute betrachtet wurde, wird sie doch eher als primitiver Walddämon gesehen.

claims.statement: All three names serve to scare children and denote a female wood sprite with shaggy, fluttering hair, large fiery eyes and very big teeth.
claims.statement_id: Ketiga nama itu dipakai untuk menakuti anak-anak dan menunjuk roh hutan perempuan berambut kusut berkibar, bermata besar menyala, dan bergigi sangat besar.
claims.quote: All three names are used to scare children and denote a female wood sprite with shaggy fluttering hair, large fiery eyes and very big teeth.

claims.statement: Dain, Dwalin (also Dvalin or Dvalar), Duneyr and Durathror are four stags in Norse (nordischen) mythology belonging to the animals of the world tree Yggdrasil.
claims.statement_id: Dain, Dwalin (juga Dvalin atau Dvalar), Duneyr, dan Durathror adalah empat rusa dalam mitologi Nordik (nordischen) yang termasuk hewan-hewan di pohon dunia Yggdrasil.
claims.quote: Dain, Dwalin (auch Dvalin oder Dvalar), Duneyr und Durathror sind vier Hirsche in der nordischen Mythologie, die zu den Tieren am Weltenbaum Yggdrasil gehören.

claims.statement: Dåin, Dvalin, Dunøyr and Duratro (Old Norse Dáinn, Dvalinn, Duneyrr, Duraþrór) are four deer that, per Gylfaginning (Gylvaginning) in the Younger Edda, run about Yggdrasil's branches and graze its foliage.
claims.statement_id: Dåin, Dvalin, Dunøyr, dan Duratro (Nordik Kuno: Dáinn, Dvalinn, Duneyrr, Duraþrór) adalah empat rusa yang menurut Gylfaginning (Gylvaginning) dalam Edda Muda berlari di dahan pohon dunia Yggdrasil dan merumput di dedaunannya.
claims.quote: Dåin, Dvalin, Dunøyr og Duratro (norrønt: Dáinn, Dvalinn, Duneyrr og Duraþrór) er fire hjortedyr som ifølge Gylvaginning i Den yngre Edda løper omkring på greinene til verdenstreet Yggdrasil og beiter i løvverket.

claims.statement: The four stags are also mentioned in Grímnismál (Grimnesmål) in the Elder Edda.
claims.statement_id: Keempat rusa itu juga disebut dalam Grímnismál (Grimnesmål) di Edda Tua.
claims.quote: De fire hjortene omtales også i Grimnesmål i Den eldre Edda

claims.statement: The stags belong to the description of the many animals in Yggdrasil: the eagle Vidofnir at the top with the hawk Verfolne between its eyes, the serpent Nidhogg coiled round its root and the squirrel Ratatosk running up and down bearing hateful words.
claims.statement_id: Rusa-rusa itu bagian dari gambaran banyak hewan di Yggdrasil: elang Vidofnir di puncak dengan elang kecil Verfolne di antara matanya, ular Nidhogg melilit akarnya, dan tupai Ratatosk berlari naik-turun membawa kata-kata kebencian.
claims.quote: Hjortene inngår i beskrivelsen av mange dyr som har tilhold i Yggdrasil. I toppen sitter ørnen Vidofnir med hauken Verfolne mellom øynene. Rundt rota på treet snor slangen Nidhogg seg, mens ekornet Ratatosk løper opp og ned og bringer hatefulle ord mellom dem.

claims.statement: Author Vera Henriksen has argued that the animals helping to destroy the world tree are 'the beginning of misery' ending in Ragnarok.
claims.statement_id: Penulis Vera Henriksen berpendapat hewan-hewan yang ikut merusak pohon dunia adalah "awal kesengsaraan" yang berakhir dengan Ragnarok.
claims.quote: Forfatteren Vera Henriksen har hevdet at dyrene som bidrar til å ødelegge verdenstreet er «begynnelsen på elendigheten» som ender i Ragnarok.

claims.statement: The Norwegian article distinguishes these stags from the dwarfs named Dåin and Dvalin.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Norwegia membedakan rusa ini dari para kurcaci bernama Dåin dan Dvalin.
claims.quote: For dvergene, se Dåin og Dvalin

claims.statement: The Elder Mother is an elder-guarding being in English and Scandinavian folklore with many names, such as the Danish Hyldemoer and the Lincolnshire Old Lady and Old Girl.
claims.statement_id: Elder Mother adalah makhluk penjaga pohon elder dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English) dan Skandinavia (Scandinavian) dengan banyak nama, seperti Hyldemoer dari Denmark (Danish) dan Old Lady atau Old Girl di Lincolnshire.
claims.quote: The Elder Mother is an elder-guarding being in English and Scandinavian folklore known by a variety of names, such as the Danish Hyldemoer ("Elder-Mother") and the Lincolnshire names Old Lady and Old Girl.

claims.statement: The Elder Mother is held to guard elder trees; until recently in parts of England and Scandinavia it was said one must first ask her before taking elder wood, or ill luck would befall the woodsman.
claims.statement_id: Elder Mother dianggap penjaga pohon elder; hingga belum lama ini di berbagai bagian Inggris (England) dan Skandinavia (Scandinavia) dikatakan bahwa untuk mengambil kayu elder orang harus meminta izinnya dulu, atau penebang akan tertimpa sial.
claims.quote: The Elder Mother is thought to be the guardian of the elder trees, and it was said, until recent times in various parts of England and Scandinavia that to take wood from the elder tree one would have to ask the Elder Mother first, or else ill luck would befall the woodsman.

claims.statement: A Somerset tale makes the Elder Mother a villain, a witch a farmer sees as an elder milking his cow; his silver bullet misses and he is chased indoors, but the old granny throws burning coal at the elder and the witch dies.
claims.statement_id: Kisah dari Somerset menjadikan Elder Mother penjahat, penyihir yang dilihat petani dalam wujud pohon elder sedang memerah sapinya; tembakan peluru peraknya meleset dan ia dikejar ke rumah, tetapi nenek tua melempar bara ke pohon elder dan penyihir itu mati.
claims.quote: Another tale, from Somerset, casts the Elder Mother as the villain, a witch that a farmer sees as an elder milking his cow. The farmer shoots at the witch with a silver bullet but misses and is chased back into the farmhouse. The old granny, however, picks up the burning coal from the fire with a shovel and throws it at the elder tree, burning cinders, and thus the witch is dead.

claims.statement: In later tales, probably under Christian influence, the image of the Flearemem (Elder Mother) shifted from protector of elder trees to a witch who may or may not mean harm.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah-kisah kemudian, kemungkinan karena pengaruh Kristen, gambaran Flearemem (Elder Mother) bergeser dari pelindung pohon elder menjadi penyihir yang bisa bermaksud jahat atau tidak.
claims.quote: Yn lettere ferhalen ferskoot de persepsje fan 'e Flearemem, grif ûnder kristlike ynfloed, fan in beskermfrouwe fan flearebeammen nei in hekse dy't al of net boasaardige bedoelings hat.

claims.statement: Thus the king and his knights were turned to stone and the witch turned herself into an elder tree.
claims.statement_id: Demikianlah raja dan para ksatrianya diubah menjadi batu, dan penyihir itu mengubah dirinya menjadi pohon elder.
claims.quote: And thus the king and his knights were turned to stone and the witch turned herself into an elder tree.

claims.statement: In Denmark the Hyldemoer or Hyldequinde ('elder woman') is a spirit like a wood nymph or dryad living in the elder tree, said to haunt or torment those who build with elder wood without asking permission.
claims.statement_id: Di Denmark (Denmark), Hyldemoer atau Hyldequinde ("perempuan elder") adalah roh mirip nimfa hutan atau dryad yang tinggal di pohon elder, dan konon menghantui atau menyiksa orang yang membangun dengan kayu elder tanpa meminta izin.
claims.quote: In Denmark, the Hyldemoer (“Elder-mother”) or Hyldequinde (“Elder-woman”) is a spirit like a wood-nymph or dryad that lives in the elder tree. The spirit is said to haunt or torment people who build from elder wood unless they ask permission first.

claims.statement: The belief in the Flearemem may well have originated in Scandinavia (Skandinaavje) and been brought to England (Ingelân) by the Vikings (Wytsingen) in the early Middle Ages, in the Danelaw era.
claims.statement_id: Mungkin saja kepercayaan akan Flearemem berasal dari Skandinavia (Skandinaavje) dan dibawa ke Inggris (Ingelân) oleh bangsa Viking (Wytsingen) pada awal Abad Pertengahan, masa Danelaw.
claims.quote: It soe skoan kinne dat it leauwen yn 'e Flearemem syn oarsprong fynt yn Skandinaavje en yn 'e Iere Midsiuwen troch de Wytsingen yn 'e tiid fan 'e Danelaw yn Ingelân brocht is.

claims.statement: In one such tale the Flearemem turns a king and his men into the Rollright Stones on the Oxfordshire–Warwickshire border, while turning herself into an elder tree.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah, Flearemem mengubah seorang raja dan anak buahnya menjadi Batu Rollright (Rollright Stones) di perbatasan Oxfordshire dan Warwickshire, sementara ia sendiri berubah menjadi pohon elder.
claims.quote: Yn ien sa'n ferhaal feroaret de Flearmem sa'n kening en syn mannen yn 'e Rollright Stones, dy't op 'e grins fan 'e Ingelske greefskippen Oxfordshire en Warwickshire steane, wylst se harsels yn in flearebeam feroaret.

claims.statement: Erawan (Thai: เอราวัณ) is the Thai (thailändische) form of the mythical elephant Airavata.
claims.statement_id: Erawan (Thai: เอราวัณ) adalah bentuk Thailand (thailändische) dari gajah mitis Airavata.
claims.quote: Erawan (in Thai: เอราวัณ) ist die thailändische Form des mythischen Elefanten Airavata.

claims.statement: Erawan is a giant elephant as big as a mountain, usually with three heads, sometimes 33, each with seven tusks.
claims.statement_id: Erawan adalah gajah raksasa sebesar gunung, biasanya berkepala tiga, kadang sampai 33, tiap kepala bergading tujuh.
claims.quote: Er ist ein riesenhafter Elefant, groß wie ein Berg. Er hat meistens drei, manchmal sogar 33 Köpfe, jeder Kopf ist mit sieben Stoßzähnen ausgestattet.

claims.statement: Erawan is the mount of Indra, the Hindu god of rain and thunder, ruler of the Tavatimsa heaven, home of 33 gods of Vedic origin.
claims.statement_id: Erawan adalah tunggangan Indra, dewa Hindu (hinduistischen) hujan dan guntur, penguasa surga Tavatimsa, kediaman 33 dewa berasal-usul Weda.
claims.quote: Er ist das Reittier des hinduistischen Gottes des Regens und des Donners Indra, dem Herrscher über den Tavatimsa-Himmel, der Wohnstatt von 33 Göttern vedischen Ursprungs.

claims.statement: Per the Traiphum Phra Ruang (14th century), in Indra's city there is an elephant named Erawan, but it is no animal, since that heaven holds no animals, only devatā; hence it is called 'Devatā Erawan'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Traiphum Phra Ruang (abad ke-14), di kota Indra ada gajah bernama Erawan, tetapi ia bukan hewan karena di surga itu tidak ada hewan, hanya devatā; maka ia disebut "Devatā Erawan".
claims.quote: In der Stadt gibt es einen Elefanten mit Namen Erawan. Allerdings ist dieser Elefant kein Tier, denn in diesem Himmel gibt es keine Tiere, er ist ausschließlich von Devatā bewohnt. So gibt es dort einen Elefanten mit Namen „Devatā Erawan“.

claims.statement: Whenever King Indra wishes to ride out for pleasure on an elephant, Devatā Erawan becomes a huge white elephant 1,200,000 wa tall with 33 heads.
claims.statement_id: Setiap kali Raja Indra ingin berkuda untuk bersenang-senang dengan menunggang gajah, Devatā Erawan menjelma menjadi gajah putih yang sangat besar, setinggi 1.200.000 wa dan berkepala 33.
claims.quote: Wann immer König Indra zum Vergnügen ausreiten möchte, und er möchte dabei auf einem Elefanten reiten, verwandelt sich „Devatā Erawan“ in einen sehr großen weißen Elefanten. Dieser Elefant ist 1.200.000 Wa hoch und hat 33 Köpfe.

claims.statement: This giant white elephant is Indra's mount and dwells in the Tavatimsa heaven; it is shown with three or more elephant heads, and the name I-rapote is also used in Thailand.
claims.statement_id: Gajah putih raksasa ini tunggangan Indra dan berada di surga Tavatimsa; ia digambarkan dengan tiga kepala gajah atau lebih, dan nama I-rapote juga dipakai di Thailand.
claims.quote: Deze reusachtige witte olifant is het rijdier van Indra en bevindt zich in de hemel Tavatimsa. Het dier wordt afgebeeld met drie of meer driekoppige olifantskoppen. Ook de naam "I-rapote" wordt in Thailand gebruikt.

claims.statement: Erawan is an important religious motif often used as ornament, as on Thai honours like the Order of Chula Chom Klao and on monuments.
claims.statement_id: Erawan adalah motif keagamaan penting dan sering dipakai sebagai ornamen, misalnya pada tanda kehormatan Thailand (Thaise) Orde Chula Chom Klao dan pada monumen.
claims.quote: De Erawan is een belangrijk religieus motief en de olifant wordt vaak als ornament gebruikt. Men ziet hem op Thaise onderscheidingen als de Orde van Chula Chom Klao waarin de erawan een centrale plaats in de keten kreeg en op monumenten.

claims.statement: In each tusk there are seven ponds, in each pond seven lotus plants; each lotus has seven flowers, each with seven petals.
claims.statement_id: Dalam setiap gading terdapat tujuh kolam, dalam setiap kolam tujuh tanaman teratai, setiap teratai bertujuh bunga, masing-masing bertujuh kelopak.
claims.quote: In jedem Stoßzahn gibt es sieben Teiche, in jedem Teich sieben Lotuspflanzen; jede Lotuspflanze hat sieben Blüten, eine jede mit sieben Blütenblättern.

claims.statement: The heads grow ever larger toward the middle; the central head is called Sudassana, Indra's throne, with a circumference of 24,000 wa.
claims.statement_id: Kepala-kepala makin besar ke arah tengah; kepala di tengah bernama Sudassana, singgasana Indra, dengan keliling 24.000 wa.
claims.quote: Die Köpfe zur Mitte hin werden immer größer, der Kopf im Zentrum heißt Sudassana. Er ist der Thron Indras und hat einen Umfang von 24.000 Wa.

claims.statement: In Norse mythology Falhófnir is a horse listed in Grímnismál and Gylfaginning among the mounts the gods ride daily to give judgements at Yggdrasil, not tied to any specific god.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Falhófnir adalah kuda yang tercantum dalam Grímnismál dan Gylfaginning di antara tunggangan para dewa yang setiap hari pergi memberi keputusan di Yggdrasil, tanpa dikaitkan dengan dewa tertentu.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Falhófnir (Old Norse: [ˈfɑlˌhoːvnez̠] ) is a horse listed in both Grímnismál and Gylfaginning among the steeds ridden by the gods each day when they go to make judgements at Yggdrasil. However, in both stanzas Falhófnir is not assigned to any specific deity.

claims.statement: The Danish article glosses Falhófnir as 'hairy hoof' or 'hidden hoof'; it is one of the stallions the Æsir (aserne) ride to Yggdrasil, and no stanza names its owner, unlike Sleipnir (Sleipner) and Freyfaxi (Frejfaxe).
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Denmark mengartikan nama Falhófnir sebagai "kuku berbulu" atau "kuku tersembunyi"; ia salah satu kuda jantan yang ditunggangi para Æsir (aserne) ke Yggdrasil, dan tak satu bait pun menyebut pemiliknya, berbeda dengan Sleipnir (Sleipner) dan Freyfaxi (Frejfaxe).
claims.quote: Falhófnir (norrønt for "behåret hov" eller "skjult hov") er en hest i nordisk mytologi, som bliver nævnt i både Grímnismál og Gylfaginning som en af de hingste, som aserne rider på hver dag, når drager til Yggdrasil for at dømme ting. I ingen af stanzaerne bliver ejerskabet af hesten tilskrevet til en bestemt gud, som det er tilfældet med bl.a. Sleipner og Frejfaxe.

claims.statement: Gylfaginning (Brodeur's translation) lists the Æsir's steeds: Sleipnir, Odin's eight-footed best, then Gladr, Gyllir, Glenr, Skeidbrimir, Silfrintoppr, Sinir, Gisl, Falhófnir, Gulltoppr and Léttfeti.
claims.statement_id: Gylfaginning (terjemahan Brodeur) mendaftar kuda para Æsir: Sleipnir yang terbaik milik Odin dan berkaki delapan, lalu Gladr, Gyllir, Glenr, Skeidbrimir, Silfrintoppr, Sinir, Gisl, Falhófnir, Gulltoppr, dan Léttfeti.
claims.quote: These are the names of the Æsir's steeds: Sleipnir is best, which Odin has; he has eight feet. The second is Gladr, the third Gyllir, the fourth Glenr, the fifth Skeidbrimir, the sixth Silfrintoppr, the seventh Sinir, the eighth Gisl, the ninth Falhófnir, the tenth Gulltoppr, the eleventh Léttfeti.

claims.statement: A Fängge (plural Fänggen) is a wood sprite or kind of wild woman in German folklore, found in the German-speaking Alpine region and further north in Bavaria (Upper Palatinate).
claims.statement_id: Fängge (jamak Fänggen) adalah roh hutan atau sejenis perempuan liar dalam cerita rakyat Jerman (German), dikenal di wilayah Alpen (Alpine) berbahasa Jerman hingga Bayern (Bavaria) utara, Oberpfalz (Upper Palatinate).
claims.quote: A Fängge (plural Fänggen ) is a wood sprite or a subtype of wild women in German folklore, found in German-speaking parts of the Alpine Region into more northerly non-Alpine parts of Bavaria (Upper Palatinate).

claims.statement: The Fängge is conceived as strictly female, a hairy, ugly giantess (counterpart of the moss-grown male giant or wild man), though the gender line is vague.
claims.statement_id: Fängge dibayangkan khusus perempuan, raksasa perempuan berbulu dan buruk rupa (padanan raksasa lelaki atau lelaki liar berlumut), meski batas jenis kelaminnya kabur.
claims.quote: The Fängge has been conceived of strictly as female, a hairy, ugly giantess (counterpart of the moss-grown male giant or wild man). However, the gender demarcation is vague.

claims.statement: In the broad sense Fängge (also Wildfanggen) means a nature spirit, giant or dwarfish, in Bavaria (Upper Palatinate), Liechtenstein, Tyrol and Switzerland.
claims.statement_id: Dalam arti luas, Fängge (juga Wildfanggen) menunjuk roh alam, raksasa maupun kerdil, di Bayern (Bavaria; Upper Palatinate), Liechtenstein, Tirol (Tyrol), dan Swiss (Switzerland).
claims.quote: Fängge in the broad sense refers to a nature spirit, either gigantic or dwarfish, in Bavaria (Upper Palatinate), Liechtenstein, Tyrol, as well as in Switzerland

claims.statement: The Fankerl is a bearded dwarf with flashy red eyes on the Pfreimd River in Upper Palatinate lore, Bavaria, counted as a type of Fängge.
claims.statement_id: Fankerl adalah kurcaci berjanggut bermata merah menyala yang tinggal di Sungai Pfreimd menurut cerita Oberpfalz (Upper Palatinate), Bayern (Bavaria), dan digolongkan sebagai Fängge.
claims.quote: The Fankerl (plural Fankerln ) is a type of bearded dwarf with flashy red eyes living on the Pfreimd River according to the lore of the Upper Palatinate, Bavaria, and it is counted as a type of Fängge.

claims.statement: Per the lore of Tyrol and the Bavarian Alps, the Fängge (Fangga) is a giantess as tall as a tree.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita Tirol (Tyrol) dan Alpen Bayern (Bavarian Alps), Fängge (Fangga) adalah raksasa perempuan setinggi pohon.
claims.quote: The Fängge (var. Fangga ) is a giantess as tall as a tree, according to the lore of Tyrol and the Bavarian Alps.

claims.statement: The Fänggen (singular Fangga, Fanggin), also Fänken, Fenggen and Fanggen, are legendary beings of southern Germany (Süddeutschland), Austria (Österreich) and South Tyrol (Südtirol); by author, time and place they are giant forest demons, witch figures or tree-bound forest fairies.
claims.statement_id: Fänggen (tunggal Fangga, Fanggin), juga Fänken, Fenggen, dan Fanggen, adalah makhluk legenda di Jerman selatan (Süddeutschland), Austria (Österreich), dan Tirol Selatan (Südtirol); tergantung pengarang, masa, dan tempat mereka digambarkan sebagai setan hutan raksasa, sosok penyihir, atau peri hutan yang terikat pada pohon.
claims.quote: Die Fänggen (Sing.: Fangga; Fanggin), welche auch Fänken, Fenggen und Fanggen genannt werden, sind Wesen und Sagengestalten in Süddeutschland, Österreich und Südtirol. Je nach Autor, Zeit und Ort werden sie entweder als riesenhafte Walddämonen, als Hexengestalten oder auch als baumverbundene Waldfeen beschrieben.

claims.statement: Johann Nepomuk von Alpenburg (1857) describes the Fänggen as huge, hairy all over, with a distorted face, a mouth stretched from ear to ear and black hair hung with tree-beard.
claims.statement_id: Johann Nepomuk von Alpenburg (1857) melukiskan Fänggen sangat besar, berbulu sekujur tubuh, wajah berkerut, mulut terentang dari telinga ke telinga, rambut hitam penuh lumut janggut pohon.
claims.quote: riesengroß, am ganzen Körper behaart, geborstet, das Antlitz verzerrt, der Mund von einem Ohre zum anderen gezogen, das schwarze Haupthaar hängt voll Baumbart

claims.statement: They are said to have secret knowledge, such as the hidden powers of plants, which can be coaxed from them once drunk; most have names like Rauhrinda and Stutzförcha; in legends they are often reduced to bogeys for children or shown as stupid.
claims.statement_id: Mereka konon memiliki pengetahuan rahasia, misalnya tentang khasiat tersembunyi tumbuhan, yang bisa dikorek setelah mereka dibuat mabuk; kebanyakan punya nama diri seperti Rauhrinda dan Stutzförcha; dalam legenda mereka sering dijadikan momok anak atau digambarkan bodoh.
claims.quote: Es heißt, dass sie über geheimes Wissen verfügen, wie zum Beispiel jenes über die geheimen Kräfte der Pflanzen, das man ihnen entlocken kann, wenn man sie erst betrunken gemacht hat. Auch sollen die meisten über Eigennamen verfügen, wie zum Beispiel Rauhrinda und Stutzförcha. In Sagen werden sie häufig zum Kinderschreck deklassiert oder als dumm dargestellt.

claims.statement: They appear alone or in groups, but their lives are always bound to a particular forest; if it disappears, say through felling, they disappear too.
claims.statement_id: Mereka muncul sendirian maupun berkelompok, tetapi hidupnya selalu terikat pada hutan tertentu; bila hutan itu hilang, misalnya karena ditebang, mereka pun lenyap.
claims.quote: Sie sollen sowohl solitär, als auch in Gruppen auftreten, wie in den oben beschriebenen Sagen, sind dabei aber stets an einen bestimmten Wald mit ihrem Leben gebunden. Würde besagter Wald verschwinden, etwa durch Abholzung, würden auch sie verschwinden.

claims.statement: Besides giant Fänggen, some legends know small dwarf-like Fängge living in rock clefts and mounds called Fänggenlöcher.
claims.statement_id: Selain Fänggen raksasa, dalam beberapa legenda ada pula Fängge kecil seperti kurcaci yang tinggal di celah batu dan gundukan tanah yang disebut Fänggenlöcher.
claims.quote: Neben den riesenhaften Fänggen existieren in manchen Sagen und Erzählungen auch kleine, zwerghafte Fängge. Diese Winzlinge sollen in Felsenklüften und Erdhügeln, die Fänggenlöcher genannt werden, hausen.

claims.statement: Another trait, surely added with Christianisation, is that the Fänggen, like other pagan figures, can be driven off by the ringing of a church bell.
claims.statement_id: Ciri lain yang pasti baru muncul seiring Kristenisasi: Fänggen, seperti sosok pagan lain, dapat diusir dengan dentang lonceng gereja.
claims.quote: Ein weiteres Merkmal der Fänggen, das sicherlich erst im Zuge der Christianisierung hinzukam, ist, dass man sie, wie auch andere heidnische Gestalten durch das Läuten einer Kirchenglocke vertreiben kann.

claims.statement: Their eyes are dark and coal-black but sometimes glow and flash; their voice is a man's, rough and coarse; they wear aprons of wildcat fur, jackets of tree bark and shaggy fox-skin aprons.
claims.statement_id: Mata mereka gelap sehitam arang tetapi kadang menyala dan memancarkan kilat; suara mereka suara lelaki yang kasar; pakaiannya celemek kulit kucing hutan, jaket kulit kayu, dan celemek bulu rubah.
claims.quote: Die Augen sind dunkel und nachtschwarz wie Kohlen, glühen aber auch zu Zeiten und sprühen Blitze – die Stimme ist Mannesstimme, rauh und ungefüge. Ihre Kleidung sind Schurze von Wildkatzenpelzen, Joppen von Baumrinden und Zottelschurze von Füchsen und anderm Getier.

claims.statement: The small Fängge are often equated with dwarfs and gnomes but, despite their size, are immensely strong; they tame chamois and wolves, drink their milk and even ride them.
claims.statement_id: Fängge kecil sering disamakan dengan kurcaci dan gnome tetapi, meski bertubuh kecil, sangat kuat; mereka menjinakkan chamois dan serigala, meminum susunya, bahkan menungganginya.
claims.quote: Sie werden oft mit den Zwergen, Gnomen und derlei gleichgesetzt, sollen aber, trotz ihrer geringen Körpergröße, über gewaltige Kräfte verfügen. Außerdem heißt es, dass sie Gämse und Wölfe zähmen, deren Milch trinken und sie gar als Reittiere nutzen sollen.

claims.statement: A Tyrolean (Tiroler) legend: in the forest from Nassereit to Stra lived a Fangg as tall as a middling tree, always lurking for people; when she caught little boys she snuffed them up her nose.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Tirol (Tiroler): di hutan antara Nassereit dan Stra tinggal seekor Fangg setinggi pohon sedang yang selalu mengintai manusia, dan bila menangkap anak lelaki kecil, ia mengisapnya ke dalam hidungnya seperti tembakau.
claims.quote: „Im Walde, der von Nassereit nach Stra sich zieht, hauste eine Fangg, welche von der Größe eines mittelmäßigen Baumes war. Sie lauerte stets auf Menschen, und wenn sie kleine Buben zu fassen bekam, so schnupfte sie dieselben in ihre Nase

claims.statement: The Fenixmännlein (also Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, Fenesleute) are earth sprites and dwarfs of German folklore, once known in Silesia, especially the Oderské vrchy and Hrubý Jeseník, and in the Saxon part of Lusatia.
claims.statement_id: Fenixmännlein (juga Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, Fenesleute) adalah roh tanah dan kurcaci dari cerita rakyat Jerman (German), dahulu dikenal di Silesia, terutama Oderské vrchy dan Hrubý Jeseník, serta bagian Lusatia milik Sachsen (Saxony).
claims.quote: are earth sprites and dwarves from German folklore. They were historically known in Silesia, particularly in the Oderské vrchy and Hrubý Jeseník as well as in the part of Lusatia belonging to Saxony.

claims.statement: Derivation from the Venedigermännlein ('little Venetian men') is supported since both are bigger than dwarfs but smaller than humans; the Fenixmännlein live collectively in hills and shrubbery.
claims.statement_id: Asal nama dari Venedigermännlein ("lelaki kecil dari Venesia") didukung fakta bahwa keduanya lebih besar dari kurcaci tetapi lebih kecil dari manusia; Fenixmännlein hidup berkelompok di bukit dan semak.
claims.quote: The latter option is supported by the fact that both Fenixmännlein and Venedigermännlein are supposed to be bigger than dwarves (German Zwerge, sg. Zwerg) but smaller than humans. The Fenixmännlein are collective beings dwelling in hills and shrubbery.

claims.statement: Inside the mountains they hold big parties; they are said to own the original Silesian streuselkuchen recipe, and when they bake in their caves smoke rises from earth holes.
claims.statement_id: Di dalam gunung mereka berpesta besar; mereka konon pemilik asli resep kue streusel Silesia (Silesian streuselkuchen), dan saat mereka memanggang di gua, asap naik dari lubang tanah.
claims.quote: Inside the mountains, they throw big parties. The Fenismannla (pl. Mannla = little men in Silesian German) are said to be the original owners of the recipe for Silesian streuselkuchen. When the Fänismännchen (sg., pl.;Männchen = little man) are baking cake in their caves, smoke is rising from earth holes and from beneath clods.

claims.statement: The Fenixmännlein occasionally swap human children for their own, left behind as changelings.
claims.statement_id: Fenixmännlein kadang menukar anak manusia dengan anak mereka sendiri, yang ditinggalkan sebagai anak tukar.
claims.quote: The Fenixmännlein are known to occasionally exchange human children for their own which are left behind as changelings.

claims.statement: A ploughboy who asked for cake was at once handed a cabbage cake with linseed oil by an invisible hand, threatened to eat it on an iron table; he used his ploughshare as that table.
claims.statement_id: Seorang pembajak yang meminta kue segera diberi kue kubis berlapis minyak biji rami oleh tangan tak terlihat, dengan ancaman harus memakannya di atas meja besi; ia memakai mata bajaknya sebagai meja besi.
claims.quote: Immediately, an invisible hand gave him a Krautkuchen (cabbage cake) coated with green linseed oil. At the same time, he got threatened to eat this cake on a table made from iron or else he would be done for. The ploughboy fulfilled the condition by using his ploughshare as the iron table.

claims.statement: The Fenixmännlein's cake may turn to lead in the stomach, to dust (that of the Fenesleute of the Fenesloch), or to gold.
claims.statement_id: Kue Fenixmännlein bisa berubah menjadi timah di dalam perut, menjadi debu (kue Fenesleute dari Fenesloch), atau menjadi emas.
claims.quote: The cake of the Fenixmannla turns to lead inside the stomach. The Krautplatz (cabbage cake) of the Fenesleute dwelling in the Fenesloch (Fenes Hole) turns to dust. The cake of the Fenixmännchen might also turn to gold.

claims.statement: Fenixmännlein (Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, Fenisleute) are a group of Silesian (schlesischer) dwarfish demons thought related to earth spirits and dwarfs; like most nature spirits they live near people and try to swap human children with changelings, but are rarely malicious.
claims.statement_id: Fenixmännlein (Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, Fenisleute) adalah kelompok setan kerdil Silesia (schlesischer) yang dianggap berkerabat dengan roh tanah dan kurcaci; seperti kebanyakan roh alam mereka tinggal dekat manusia dan mencoba menukar anak manusia dengan anak tukar, tetapi jarang jahat.
claims.quote: Als Fenixmännlein (Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, Fenisleute) bezeichnet man eine Gruppe schlesischer zwergenhafter Dämonen, die mit den Erdgeistern und Zwergen verwandt sein sollen, da sie denselben Beschäftigungen nachgehen. Wie die meisten Naturgeister leben sie in menschlicher Nähe und versuchen, die Kinder der Menschen mit ihren Wechselbälgern zu vertauschen. Selten sind sie bösartig.

claims.statement: The rescuer of an abducted woman must ride as fast as possible, throwing flax, a comb and soap behind him.
claims.statement_id: Penyelamat perempuan yang diculik harus berkuda secepatnya sambil melempar rami, sisir, dan sabun ke belakang.
claims.quote: The rescuer will need to ride his horse as fast as he can, all the while throwing behind him flax (the dwarves must pull) a comb (the dwarves must heckle the flax with) and soap (the dwarves will slip on).

claims.statement: In Austrian Silesia the Fenesleute left because people began adding parsley, which they could not stand, to their food, and because of the railways.
claims.statement_id: Di Silesia Austria, Fenesleute meninggalkan negeri karena orang mulai menambahkan peterseli ke masakan, yang tak mereka tahan, dan karena hadirnya jalur kereta api.
claims.quote: In Austrian Silesia, the Fenesleute have moved out of the country. This happened because people started adding parsley to their dishes which they were unable to tolerate. The introduction railways also made the Fenesleute migrate

claims.statement: In Lusatia the Venusmännel or Feensmännel moved west after Ostritz got its bell tower, as the dwarfs could not stand the big bell.
claims.statement_id: Di Lusatia, Venusmännel atau Feensmännel pindah ke barat setelah Ostritz memiliki menara lonceng, karena para kurcaci tak tahan suara lonceng besarnya.
claims.quote: In Lusatia, the Venusmännel or Feensmännel migrated westwards after Ostritz had got its bell tower. The dwarves could not stand the sound of the large bell in particular.

claims.statement: The Fenixmännlein especially like abducting women in childbed to the Fenixmannlaberg to nurse their children or wash.
claims.statement_id: Fenixmännlein terutama suka menculik perempuan yang baru melahirkan dan membawanya ke Fenixmannlaberg untuk mengasuh anak-anak mereka atau mencuci.
claims.quote: The Fenixmännlein particularly like abducting women in childbed, carrying them off to the Fenixmannlaberg (Fenix Men Mountain) to care for their children or for washing.

claims.statement: Not only the male Fenixmännlein can bake; their female counterparts, the Venusweiblein, can too.
claims.statement_id: Bukan hanya Fenixmännlein lelaki yang pandai memanggang; padanan perempuan mereka, Venusweiblein, juga.
claims.quote: But not only the male Fenixmännlein know how to bake, their female equivalent, the Venusweiblein (sg., pl.; Weiblein = little woman), do too.

claims.statement: The Feuermann ('fire man'; also Brennender, Brünnling, Züsler, Glühender, glühende Männer) is a fiery ghost of German folklore, unlike the will-o'-the-wisp (Irrlicht) in size: Feuermänner are big, Irrlichter small.
claims.statement_id: Feuermann ("manusia api"; juga Brennender, Brünnling, Züsler, Glühender, glühende Männer) adalah hantu berapi dari cerita rakyat Jerman (German) yang berbeda dari will-o'-the-wisp (Irrlicht) karena ukurannya: Feuermänner agak besar, Irrlichter agak kecil.
claims.quote: is a fiery ghost from German folklore, which is different from the will-o'-the-wisp (German Irrlicht) owing to its size: Feuermänner are rather big, while Irrlichter are rather small.

claims.statement: Some are humanlike, such as a skeleton blazing inside or a leaden manikin with fire under its mantle; others a black man in a pillar of fire; it can change its height at will from gigantic to tiny.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian digambarkan mirip manusia, seperti kerangka yang menyala dari dalam atau lelaki kecil bermantel timah dengan api di bawahnya; ada pula lelaki hitam di dalam tiang api; ia dapat mengubah tingginya sesuka hati dari raksasa hingga kecil.
claims.quote: Some are described as rather humanoid, such as a human skeleton whose insides are blazing with fire, or as a leaden manikin wearing a leaden mantle blazing with fire underneath. Another description is of a black man inside a tall, wide pillar of fire, or a Feuermann who is half black, half fiery. It is able to change its height at will, varying from gigantic to diminutive.

claims.statement: The Feuermann may also appear nearly shapeless, as a (sometimes giant) sheaf of straw, a big floating light, a fireball, a pyramid, a snake or a fiery wheel; it is very fast and can rise to hover above the treetops.
claims.statement_id: Feuermann juga bisa tampil hampir tanpa bentuk, seperti berkas jerami (kadang raksasa), cahaya besar melayang, bola api, piramida, ular, atau roda api; ia sangat cepat dan dapat naik ke udara melayang di atas pucuk pohon.
claims.quote: Alternatively, the Feuermann also appears more or less shapeless like a (sometimes gigantic) sheaf or bundle of straw, a big floating light, a fiery ball, a pyramid, a snake, or a fiery wheel. The Feuermann is very quick and able to rise in the air so that it hovers above the treetops.

claims.statement: The Feuermann is seen as a sinner haunting the earth to atone for its life's sins; often a Grenzfrevler who moved a boundary stone with criminal intent and is damned to haunt that boundary.
claims.statement_id: Feuermann dianggap pendosa yang bergentayangan di bumi untuk menebus dosa semasa hidup; sering ia seorang Grenzfrevler yang memindahkan batu batas dengan niat jahat sehingga jiwanya dikutuk menghantui batas itu.
claims.quote: It is seen as a sinner remaining hauntingly on earth to repent for its sins during lifetime. Frequently, the Feuermann is a so-called Grenzfrevler (sg., pl.) or boundary sinner who has moved a boundary stone or similar landmark with criminal intent, thus damning the soul to haunt the very boundary it unlawfully changed in life.

claims.statement: The Feuermann appears only in the evening or at night, preferably in fields, especially field borders, and meadows, particularly swampy ones.
claims.statement_id: Feuermann hanya muncul pada sore atau malam hari, terutama di ladang, khususnya batas ladang, dan padang rumput, terutama yang berawa.
claims.quote: The Feuermann appears only at evening or at night, preferably at fields, particularly field borders, and meadows, especially swampy ones.

claims.statement: The Feuerputz, also called Brünnling, Feuerpütz, Glühender, Züsler, but most often Feuermann, is a fiery spook and legendary figure.
claims.statement_id: Feuerputz, juga disebut Brünnling, Feuerpütz, Glühender, Züsler, tetapi paling sering Feuermann, adalah hantu berapi dan tokoh legenda.
claims.quote: Der Feuerputz, der auch Brünnling, Feuerpütz, Feurputz, Glühender, Züsler, am häufigsten aber Feuermann genannt wird, ist ein feuriger Spuk und eine Sagengestalt.

claims.statement: Feuermänner are souls who sinned in life and must now atone; their fiery form is their purgatory.
claims.statement_id: Feuermänner adalah jiwa yang berdosa semasa hidup dan kini harus menebusnya; wujud berapi mereka adalah api penyucian mereka.
claims.quote: Feuermänner sind Seelen, die sich im Leben versündigt haben und dies nun abbüßen müssen. Ihre feurige Erscheinung ist also ihr Fegefeuer.

claims.statement: Usually harmless, the Feuermann may help by lighting the way at night for a small coin or thanks such as 'Vergelt's Gott'; such a blessing redeems the burning sinner.
claims.statement_id: Biasanya tak berbahaya, Feuermann bisa menolong dengan menerangi jalan pada malam hari demi sedikit uang atau ucapan terima kasih seperti "Vergelt's Gott" ("semoga Tuhan membalasnya"); berkat semacam itu menebus pendosa yang terbakar itu.
claims.quote: Usually harmless, the Feuermann can also appear helpful to humans by showing and illuminating them the way at night for a small sum of money or a word of gratitude such as "Vergelt's Gott" ("May God reward it") or "Bezahl dir's Gott (soviel Mal wie du's nötig hast)" ("May God repay you (as many times as you need)"). Such a blessing redeems the burning sinner

claims.statement: A Feuermann turns malicious when refused a promised reward or taking revenge on a prankster; then it leads people astray and leaps onto their backs (aufhocken).
claims.statement_id: Feuermann menjadi jahat bila imbalan yang dijanjikan tidak diberikan atau bila membalas orang yang mempermainkannya; ia lalu menyesatkan orang dan melompat ke punggung mereka (aufhocken).
claims.quote: A malicious Feuermann can be experienced when it has helped out a human and is refused the promised reward or when it takes revenge on a human who has played a prank on it. Then, the Feuermann leads astray, practices "aufhocken"

claims.statement: Touching the Feuermann's hand is dangerous; so one should offer an object instead of one's hand, as a black handprint will be burnt where it touched.
claims.statement_id: Menyentuh tangan Feuermann berbahaya; karena itu orang sebaiknya menyodorkan benda alih-alih tangannya, sebab akan tertinggal cap tangan hitam yang terbakar di tempat yang disentuhnya.
claims.quote: It is dangerous to touch the Feuermann's hand. Thus, one should always give an object instead of one's hand as one will find a black handprint burnt on it where the Feuermann has touched.

claims.statement: A simple 'Vergelt's Gott' is said to be enough to redeem the Feuermann.
claims.statement_id: Ucapan sederhana "Vergelt's Gott" konon sudah cukup untuk menebus Feuermann.
claims.quote: Schon ein schlichtes „Vergelt's Gott“ soll dabei ausreichen, um den Feuermann zu erlösen.

claims.statement: Rarer forms are a fiery, sometimes headless rider on a fiery horse and a fiery ploughman with fiery horse and plough.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan yang lebih jarang adalah penunggang berapi, kadang tanpa kepala, di atas kuda berapi, dan pembajak berapi dengan kuda dan bajak berapi.
claims.quote: Rarer appearances are that of a fiery, sometimes headless rider on a fiery horse and that of a fiery ploughman with fiery horse and plough.

claims.statement: Such a blessing redeems the burning sinner, as do prayers and masses, so Feuermänner approach on hearing a prayer; swearing drives them away.
claims.statement_id: Berkat semacam itu menebus pendosa yang terbakar, begitu pula doa dan misa, sehingga Feuermänner mendekat bila mendengar doa; sebaliknya umpatan mengusir mereka.
claims.quote: Such a blessing redeems the burning sinner, as do prayers and masses because of which Feuermänner draw near upon hearing a prayer. Swearing drives them away instead.

claims.statement: Or it follows the person and sets the straw on their wagon or even their house on fire.
claims.statement_id: Atau ia mengikuti orang itu dan membakar jerami di gerobak bahkan rumahnya.
claims.quote: or follows the person and sets the straw on their wagon or even their house ablaze.

claims.statement: Other possible identities of the Feuermann include a sacristan who stole from the collection bag, a murderous arsonist, a traitor to his country and other evildoers.
claims.statement_id: Identitas lain Feuermann termasuk koster yang mencuri uang kantong kolekte, pembakar pembunuh, pengkhianat negeri, dan berbagai penjahat lain.
claims.quote: Other possible identities of the Feuermann include a sacristan who has stolen money from the collection bag, a murderous incendiary, a traitor of his country, and several other kinds of evildoers.

claims.statement: The Finngálkn is a fabulous beast, human above and animal below (also called Kentári, centaur); the word also denotes the offspring of a fox and a cat.
claims.statement_id: Finngálkn adalah makhluk dongeng, manusia di atas dan hewan di bawah (juga disebut Kentári, kentaur); kata finngálkn juga dipakai untuk keturunan rubah dan kucing.
claims.quote: Finngálkn er furðusagnakvikindi, maður að ofan en dýr að neðan (einnig kallað Kentári). Finngálkn er einnig haft um afkvæmi tófu og kattar.

claims.statement: Per Jón Árnason's folktales (Þjóðsögum Jóns Árnasonar), the finngálkn is the beast a cat and fox beget, very fierce, more harmful to sheep than any other predator and hardest of all to shoot; no bullet works on it but a silver button or bullet.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kumpulan cerita Jón Árnason (Þjóðsögum Jóns Árnasonar), finngálkn adalah hewan hasil kawin kucing dan rubah, sangat buas, lebih berbahaya bagi domba daripada pemangsa lain, dan paling sulit ditembak; tak ada peluru yang mempan kecuali kancing atau peluru perak.
claims.quote: Finngálkn er það dýr kallað, sem köttur og tófa geta saman. Er það grimmt mjög, og öllum vargi skaðlegra fyrir sauðfé manna, og skotharðast allra dýra. Vinnur engin kúla á Finngálknið, og verður það ekki skotið nema með silfurhnapp eða silfurkúlu.

claims.statement: The Finngálkn is a fabulous beast named in several legendary sagas (fornaldarsagor), a chimera, usually a mix of human and animal.
claims.statement_id: Finngálkn adalah hewan dongeng yang disebut dalam beberapa saga legendaris (fornaldarsagor), sejenis kimera, biasanya campuran manusia dan hewan.
claims.quote: Finngálkn är ett fabeldjur som omtalas i flera fornaldarsagor. Det rör sig om en chimär; oftast en blandning mellan människa och djur.

claims.statement: In the 12th-century Icelandic (isländska) translation of the bestiary Physiologus, surviving only in two 13th-century fragments, finngálkn is said to be a centaur (onocentaurus).
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Islandia (isländska) bestiari Physiologus dari abad ke-12, yang hanya tersisa dalam dua fragmen abad ke-13, finngálkn disebut kentaur (onocentaurus).
claims.quote: I den isländska översättningen av bestiariet Physiologus, gjord på 1100-talet men endast bevarad i två 1200-talsfragment, sägs finngálkn vara en kentaur

claims.statement: Örvar-Odds saga says Grímhildr, mother of Ögmundr Eyþjófsbani, once turned into a finngálkn: her head human, her hind body an animal's, with very large claws and a huge tail.
claims.statement_id: Örvar-Odds saga menyebut Grímhildr, ibu Ögmundr Eyþjófsbani, pernah berubah menjadi finngálkn: kepalanya seperti manusia, tubuh belakangnya hewan, bercakar sangat besar dan berekor raksasa.
claims.quote: Om Ögmundr Eyþjófsbanis mor Grímhildr sägs i Örvar-Odds saga att hon vid en viss tidpunkt hade förvandlats till finngálkn. Hennes huvud var som en människas, men bakkroppen ett djurs. Hon hade mycket stora klor och en väldig svans.

claims.statement: Hjálmþés saga ok Ölvis mentions a female named Vargeisa, seemingly a 'horse-centaur': horse's tail and hooves, long mane, bright eyes, wide mouth and large hands.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Hjálmþés saga ok Ölvis disebut finngálkn betina bernama Vargeisa, tampaknya "kentaur kuda": berekor dan berkuku kuda, bersurai panjang, bermata terang, bermulut lebar, bertangan besar.
claims.quote: En hona, lystrande till namnet Vargeisa, som tycks ha tillhört ”hästkentaurerna”, omtalas i Hjálmþés saga ok Ölvis. ”Hon hade hästsvans, hovar och lång man; ögonen var ljusa, munnen bred och händerna stora.”

claims.statement: The etymology of finngálkn is unknown; the word is associated with 'unnatural mixture'.
claims.statement_id: Etimologi kata finngálkn tidak diketahui; kata itu dikaitkan dengan "campuran yang tak wajar".
claims.quote: Etymologin för ordet finngálkn är okänd. Ordet associerar till ”onaturlig blandning”.

claims.statement: In the Middle Ages Finngálkn was a Norse (norrönt) name for the constellation Sagittarius.
claims.statement_id: Pada Abad Pertengahan, Finngálkn adalah nama Nordik (norrönt) untuk rasi Sagitarius (Sagittarius).
claims.quote: Under medeltiden var Finngálkn ett norrönt namn på stjärnbilden Sagittarius.

claims.statement: In Njáls saga Þorkell hákr met a finngálkn, fought it long and finally killed it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Njáls saga, Þorkell hákr bertemu finngálkn, lama bertarung dengannya, dan akhirnya membunuhnya.
claims.quote: Þá mœtti hann finngálkni og varðisk því lengi, en svá lauk með þeim, at hann drap finngálknit.

claims.statement: In Hjálmþés saga ok Ölvis Prince Hjálmþér is forced to kiss the finngálkn Vargeisa, who proves to be a bewitched princess.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Hjálmþés saga ok Ölvis, pangeran Hjálmþér terpaksa mencium finngálkn Vargeisa, yang ternyata putri yang terkena sihir.
claims.quote: Í Hjálmþés sögu og Ölvis neyðist konungssonurinn Hjálmþés til að kyssa finngálknið Vargeisu. Hún reynist þó vera prinsessa í álögum.

claims.statement: Sagittarius was often shown as an archer centaur, so the constellation, besides Bogmaðr or Skyti, came to be called Finngálkn.
claims.statement_id: Sagitarius sering digambarkan sebagai kentaur pemanah, sehingga rasi ini, selain disebut Bogmaðr atau Skyti, juga dinamai Finngálkn.
claims.quote: Sagittarius avbildades ofta som en bågskjutande kentaur, varför denna stjärnbild – förutom de mer korrekta benämningarna Bogmaðr eller Skyti – också kom att kallas Finngálkn.

claims.statement: Fjalar (Old Norse Fjalarr, 'deceiver') is the mythical red rooster said to herald the onset of Ragnarök in Norse mythology.
claims.statement_id: Fjalar (Nordik Kuno: Fjalarr, "penipu") adalah ayam jantan merah mitis yang dikatakan menandai awal Ragnarök dalam mitologi Nordik (Norse).
claims.quote: Fjalar (Old Norse: Fjalarr [ˈfjɑlɑrː] , "deceiver") is the mythical red rooster that is said to herald the onset of Ragnarök in Norse mythology.

claims.statement: The Old Norse name Fjalarr has been rendered 'deceiver' or 'hider', probably from a reconstructed Proto-Norse *felaraʀ.
claims.statement_id: Nama Nordik Kuno Fjalarr diterjemahkan "penipu" atau "penyembunyi" dan mungkin berasal dari bentuk Proto-Nordik (Proto-Norse) *felaraʀ.
claims.quote: The Old Norse name Fjalarr has been translated as 'deceiver' or 'hider'. It probably derives from an earlier Proto-Norse form reconstructed as *felaraʀ.

claims.statement: Three other unrelated figures are called Fjalar: an alias of Suttungr in Hávamál's version of Odin's theft of the mead of poetry, one of the dwarfs who made the mead from Kvasir's blood in Skáldskaparmál.
claims.statement_id: Tiga tokoh lain yang tak berkaitan juga bernama Fjalar: nama lain Suttungr dalam versi Hávamál tentang pencurian mead puisi oleh Odin, dan salah satu kurcaci pembuat mead puisi dari darah Kvasir dalam Skáldskaparmál.
claims.quote: Three other unrelated figures bear the name Fjalar in Norse mythology. It is an alias of Suttungr in the Hávamál ('Sayings of the High One') version of Odin's theft of the mead of poetry. Fjalar is also the name of one of the dwarfs who made the mead of poetry from the blood of Kvasir in Skáldskaparmál ('The Language of Poetry').

claims.statement: Peter H. Salus and Paul B. Taylor argue that of the four probably only the dwarf is really named Fjalar; the cock and the two giants are so called for their cunning.
claims.statement_id: Peter H. Salus dan Paul B. Taylor berpendapat dari keempatnya mungkin hanya sang kurcaci yang benar-benar bernama Fjalar; ayam jantan dan kedua raksasa disebut Fjalar karena kelicikan mereka.
claims.quote: Peter H. Salus and Paul B. Taylor argue that "of these four, probably only one (the dwarf) is actually named Fjalar, the cock and the two giants are called Fjalar because of their cunning."

claims.statement: In Völuspá Fjalar is shown as a beautiful red rooster crowing in the onset of Ragnarök near the herdsman Eggþér, who joyfully strikes his harp.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Völuspá, Fjalar digambarkan sebagai ayam jantan merah yang indah yang berkokok menandai awal Ragnarök, di dekat gembala Eggþér yang dengan riang memetik harpanya.
claims.quote: In Völuspá (Prophecy of the Völva), Fjalar is portrayed as a beautiful red rooster who crows the onset of Ragnarök, sitting near the herdsman Eggþér who is joyfully striking his harp.

claims.statement: In Norse (nordisk) mythology (Vølvens spådom, Völuspá) Fjalar is a red rooster who crows in a tree and so heralds Ragnarok.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik (nordisk; Vølvens spådom atau Völuspá), Fjalar adalah ayam jantan merah yang berkokok di sebatang pohon dan dengan demikian menandai Ragnarok.
claims.quote: I nordisk mytologi (Vølvens spådom) er Fjalar en rød hane, der galer i et træ og dermed indvarsler Ragnarok.

claims.statement: In Hárbarðsljóð the jötunn who succeeded in deceiving Thor is also named Fjalar.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Hárbarðsljóð, jötunn yang berhasil menipu Thor juga bernama Fjalar.
claims.quote: Finally, in Hárbarðsljóð ('The Lay of Hárbarðr'), the jötunn who succeeded in deceiving Thor is also named Fjalar.

claims.statement: Völuspá 42: on the mound sat glad Egðir, herdsman of the giantess, striking his harp; above him in the gaglviðr ('gallows-wood') crowed the fair red cock called Fjalarr.
claims.statement_id: Völuspá 42: di atas gundukan duduk Egðir, gembala raksasa perempuan, memetik harpa dengan riang; di atasnya, di gaglviðr ("hutan tiang gantungan"), berkokok ayam jantan merah indah bernama Fjalarr.
claims.quote: Sat þar á haugi ok sló hörpu gýgjar hirðir glaðr Egðir; gól um hánum í gaglviði fagrrauðr hani, sá er Fjalarr heitir .

claims.statement: The Flodder (also Flodderduivel) is a tormenting spirit of West Brabant (West-Brabantse) folklore, in the Netherlands.
claims.statement_id: Flodder (juga Flodderduivel) adalah roh pengganggu dari cerita rakyat Brabant Barat (West-Brabantse), Belanda.
claims.quote: De Flodder (ook wel Flodderduivel) is een kwelgeest uit de West-Brabantse folklore.

claims.statement: The creature lives in ditches, pools and along dykes; it lurks in the water for night walkers, leaps on their backs and is carried as a lead-heavy load; once the victim reaches inhabited parts, it suddenly vanishes.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini tinggal di parit, kolam, dan sepanjang tanggul; ia mengintai pejalan malam dari air, melompat ke punggung mereka dan minta digendong sebagai beban seberat timah; begitu korban mencapai permukiman, ia tiba-tiba lenyap.
claims.quote: Het wezen houdt zich op in sloten, plassen en langs dijken. Het loert vanuit het water langs de kant op nachtelijke wandelaars, bespringt hen op de rug en laat zich vervolgens als een loodzware last meedragen. Zodra het slachtoffer de bewoonde wereld bereikt, verdwijnt de demon plots weer.

claims.statement: The Flodder owes its name to the sound it makes when rising from the water.
claims.statement_id: Flodder mendapat namanya dari bunyi yang ia timbulkan saat muncul dari air.
claims.quote: Zijn naam dankt de Flodder aan het geluid dat hij voortbrengt wanneer hij uit het water oprijst.

claims.statement: The Flodder is halfway between ghost and beast, immaterial yet visible, untouchable yet enormously heavy on the victim's back; in some Brabant (Brabantse) tales it appears as a large black dog called a hellhound (helhond).
claims.statement_id: Flodder berada di antara roh dan hewan, tak berwujud jasmani tetapi terlihat, sehingga tak dapat disentuh namun sangat berat di punggung korban; dalam beberapa legenda Brabant (Brabantse) ia muncul sebagai anjing hitam besar yang disebut anjing neraka (helhond).
claims.quote: Het houdt het midden tussen een geest en een beest. Niet stoffelijk, maar wel zichtbaar. De Flodder is dus onaantastbaar, maar weegt wel gigantisch zwaar op de rug van het slachtoffer. In sommige Brabantse sagen verschijnt de plaaggeest in de gedaante van een grote, zwarte hond, die wordt aangeduid als helhond.

claims.statement: The Frisian article also calls the Flodder or Flodderduivel a tormenting spirit of the folklore of western North Brabant (Noard-Brabân).
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Frisia juga menyebut Flodder atau Flodderduivel roh pengganggu dari cerita rakyat bagian barat Brabant Utara (Noard-Brabân).
claims.quote: De Flodder of de Flodderduivel is in kwelgeast út 'e folkloare fan it westlike part fan Noard-Brabân.

claims.statement: It is related to Lange Wapper and the Kludde of Flanders (Vlaanderen), Blauwe Gerrit of the Veluwe, the Ossaert of Zeeland and the Stoep of Gelderland; the Bahkauv of Aachen (Aken) is similar too.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini berkerabat dengan Lange Wapper dan Kludde dari Flandria (Vlaanderen), Blauwe Gerrit dari Veluwe, Ossaert dari Zeeland, dan Stoep dari Gelderland; Bahkauv dari Aachen (Aken) juga mirip.
claims.quote: Het wezen is verwant aan Lange Wapper en de Kludde uit Vlaanderen, Blauwe Gerrit van de Veluwe, de Ossaert uit Zeeland en de Stoep uit Gelderland. Ook het Bahkauv uit Aken vertoont overeenkomsten.

claims.statement: The flogdrake (Old Swedish floghdraki; Finnish louhikäärme; also elddrake or godsdrake) is a dragon type of Swedish folklore, and less so Finnish and Estonian: a wingless worm-dragon flying glowing across the sky like a streak of fire or a shooting star, living in mountain tunnels it bores.
claims.statement_id: Flogdrake (Swedia Kuno floghdraki; Finlandia louhikäärme; juga elddrake atau godsdrake) adalah jenis naga dalam cerita rakyat Swedia (Swedish), dan sedikit dalam cerita rakyat Finlandia (Finnish) dan Estonia (Estonian): naga cacing tanpa sayap yang terbang bercahaya di langit seperti garis api atau bintang jatuh, dan tinggal di terowongan gunung yang dibornya.
claims.quote: is a type of dragon in Swedish folklore, and to a lesser extent Finnish and Estonian folklore (see kratt), by analogy a variation of the Pan-European firedrake myth; it is a wingless worm-dragon that flies across the sky while glowing, looking like a streak of fire or light akin to a shooting star, while living in mountain tunnels that it bores.

claims.statement: The flogdrake is a Nordic (nordisk) dragon type chiefly from Swedish (svensk) folk belief, also Estonian-Swedish; a wingless serpent-dragon flying like a fire streak across the sky like a falling star, dwelling in mountain tunnels it bored itself.
claims.statement_id: Flogdrake adalah jenis naga Nordik (nordisk) yang terutama berasal dari kepercayaan rakyat Swedia (svensk), juga Swedia-Estonia; naga ular tanpa sayap yang terbang seperti garis api di langit seperti bintang jatuh dan tinggal di terowongan gunung yang dibornya sendiri.
claims.quote: är en nordisk typ av drake som huvudsakligen härrör svensk folktro och folkminne, därtill även estsvensk folktro. Det är en vinglös ormdrake som flyger likt en eldstrimma eller ljusfenomen över himlen likt ett stjärnfall och bor i bergstunnlar de själva borrat.

claims.statement: Swedish flogdrake derives from Old Swedish floghdraki (flughdraki), 'fly-dragon', at first only for flying dragons, a literary loan from Old Norse flugdreki.
claims.statement_id: Kata Swedia flogdrake berasal dari Swedia Kuno floghdraki (flughdraki), "naga terbang", semula untuk naga yang terbang saja, dan merupakan pinjaman sastra dari Nordik Kuno (Old Norse) flugdreki.
claims.quote: Swedish: flogdrake derives from Old Swedish: floghdraki (including the form flughdraki), meaning ”fly-dragon”, and initially referred to just flying dragons, as opposed to non-flying ones. The term is a literary loan from Old Norse: flugdreki .

claims.statement: From Old Swedish the term entered Finnish as a partial calque, louhikäärme, 'louhi serpent'.
claims.statement_id: Dari Swedia Kuno, istilah ini dipinjam ke bahasa Finlandia (Finnish) sebagai kalke parsial louhikäärme, "ular louhi".
claims.quote: From Old Swedish, the term was borrowed into Finnish as a partial calque, there becoming louhikäärme , "louhi serpent".

claims.statement: The flogdrake resembles the eastern dragon in flying without visible wings, but Germanic dragons are always evil; it comes flying in the evening sky amid sparks, like a golden stripe sweeping across it.
claims.statement_id: Flogdrake mirip naga timur karena bisa terbang tanpa sayap yang terlihat, tetapi naga Jermanik selalu digambarkan jahat; ia datang terbang di langit senja dikelilingi bunga api, tampak seperti garis keemasan yang menyapu langit.
claims.quote: Thus the flogdrake can be compared to the eastern dragon in that it can fly despite lacking any visible wings. Unlike eastern dragons, however, Germanic dragons are always portrayed as evil. It is said to come flying in the evening sky surrounded by sparks, looking like a golden stripe that sweeps across the sky.

claims.statement: It is large and seemingly limbless, said to be shaped like a steelyard balance, essentially a long tadpole.
claims.statement_id: Ia besar dan tampak tak berkaki, dan bentuknya konon mirip timbangan dacin, pada dasarnya seperti berudu panjang.
claims.quote: It is large and seems to lack limbs, but is said to resemble a steelyard balance in shape, essentially like a long tadpole.

claims.statement: Flogdrakes are said to have lived in mountains, drilling into the rock and digging large tunnels called drakarör, where they dwelt and hid their treasure.
claims.statement_id: Flogdrake konon tinggal di gunung, mengebor batuan dan menggali terowongan besar yang disebut drakarör, tempat mereka bersemayam dan menyembunyikan hartanya.
claims.quote: The flogdrakes are said to have lived in mountains. They would drill into the rock mass, thus digging large tunnels, so-called drakarör

claims.statement: Some read the fire streak as the dragon 'illuminating his goods', so revealing where the treasure or nest lies.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang menafsirkan garis api itu sebagai naga yang "menerangi hartanya", sehingga menunjukkan letak harta atau sarang naga.
claims.quote: Some interpret the fire streak phenomenon as the dragon "firing over his possessions" or "illuminating his goods", and thus pointing out where the treasure or dragon's nest is to be found.

claims.statement: Laurentius Petri perhaps used the term in its later sense as early as 1568, in his translation of Isaiah (Jesaja).
claims.statement_id: Laurentius Petri mungkin sudah memakai istilah ini dalam arti kemudiannya pada 1568, dalam terjemahan Yesaya (Jesaja).
claims.quote: Laurentius Petri använde begreppet i sin senare betydelse kanske redan 1568 i sin översättning av Jesaja

claims.statement: Through folk etymology louhikäärme later became lohikäärme (literally 'salmon serpent'), the modern Finnish (finska) word for dragon in general.
claims.statement_id: Melalui etimologi rakyat, louhikäärme kemudian menjadi lohikäärme (harfiah "ular salmon"), kata Finlandia modern (finska) untuk naga pada umumnya.
claims.quote: Genom folketymologi har louhikäärme sedermera blivit lohikäärme (bokstavligen ”laxorm”) som på modern finska är ordet för drake i allmänhet.

claims.statement: This pattern also occurs in the Baltic states and Northern Germany, where gnomes like the German-Slavic Schrat/Puk and Estonian kratt appear at night as a 'fiery dragon'.
claims.statement_id: Pola mitologis ini juga ada di negara Baltik (Baltic) dan Jerman Utara (Northern Germany), tempat roh seperti Schrat/Puk Jerman-Slavia dan kratt Estonia (Estonian) muncul pada malam hari sebagai "naga api".
claims.quote: This mythological pattern also occurs elsewhere, such as in the Baltic states and Northern Germany, where gnomes, such as the German-Slavic Schrat/Puk , and Estonian derivative kratt/puuk (Estonian Swedish: skrat), appear at night as a "fiery dragon" or thereof.

claims.statement: Petri rendered the end of Isaiah 14:29 (the seraph) as 'en brinnande floghdrake' ('a burning fly-dragon').
claims.statement_id: Petri menerjemahkan bagian akhir Yesaya 14:29 (seraf) sebagai "en brinnande floghdrake" ("naga terbang yang menyala").
claims.quote: in which Petri translated the last part as: "en brinnande floghdrake" ("a burning fly-dragon").

claims.statement: Unlike the treasure-guarding dragon, the flogdrake 'is rarely seen in its true form, but more often observed streaking through the air like a flame', wrote Leonhard Fredrik Rääf (1856).
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari naga penjaga harta, flogdrake "jarang terlihat dalam wujud aslinya, lebih sering tampak melesat di udara seperti nyala api", tulis Leonhard Fredrik Rääf (1856).
claims.quote: The flogdrake, as opposed to the treasure-guarding dragon, "is rarely seen in its true form, but more often observed streaking through the air like a flame", wrote Leonhard Fredrik Rääf (1856).

claims.statement: Fjalar and Galar are dwarfs in Norse (norrænni) mythology; they murdered Kvasir (Kvasi) and brewed the mead of poetry from his blood and honey.
claims.statement_id: Fjalar dan Galar adalah kurcaci dalam mitologi Nordik (norrænni); mereka membunuh Kvasir (Kvasi) dan membuat mead puisi dari darahnya dan madu.
claims.quote: Fjalar og Galar eru dvergar í norrænni goðafræði. Þeir myrtu Kvasi og brugguðu skáldskaparmjöðinn úr blóði hans og hunangi.

claims.statement: Galar (Old Norse Galarr) was a dwarf in Norse mythology; with his brother Fjalar he killed Kvasir (Kvase), the wisest of all, born of the peace pact between the Vanir (Vaner) and Æsir (Æser), and from his blood mixed with honey they made the mead of poetry.
claims.statement_id: Galar (Nordik Kuno Galarr) adalah kurcaci dalam mitologi Nordik; bersama saudaranya Fjalar ia membunuh Kvasir (Kvase), makhluk paling bijak yang tercipta dari perjanjian damai Vanir (Vaner) dan Æsir (Æser), dan dari darahnya yang dicampur madu mereka membuat mead puisi.
claims.quote: Galar (norrønt: Galarr) var i norrøn mytologi en dverg. Sammen med broren Fjalar drepte han den viseste av alle, skapt av fredspakten mellom Vaner og Æser, Kvase. Av hans blod blandet med honning laget de skaldskapsmjøden

claims.statement: Later, after they caused the deaths of the giant Gillingr (Gillings) and his wife, their son Suttungr (Suttungur) demanded the mead as compensation.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian, setelah mereka menyebabkan kematian raksasa Gillingr (Gillings) dan istrinya, putra mereka Suttungr (Suttungur) menuntut mead itu sebagai tebusan.
claims.quote: Síðar, er þeir höfðu valdið dauða jötunsins Gillings og konu hans, þá krafðist Suttungur sonur þeirra, mjaðarins í bætur.

claims.statement: The name Fjalar is taken to mean 'hider' or 'deceiver', and Galar 'the one who screams'.
claims.statement_id: Nama Fjalar dianggap berarti "penyembunyi" atau "penipu", dan Galar "yang berteriak".
claims.quote: Nafnið Fjalar er talið þýða „felur“ eða „svikari“ en Galar „sá sem öskrar“.

claims.statement: Austrian philologist Rudolf Simek argues that the names Galar and Fjalar were constructed by Snorri (Snorre).
claims.statement_id: Filolog Austria Rudolf Simek berpendapat nama Galar dan Fjalar diciptakan oleh Snorri (Snorre).
claims.quote: Den østerrikske filologen Rudolf Simek hevder at navnene Galar og Fjalar er konstruert av Snorre.

claims.statement: The story of the origin of poetry and Suttungr's mead is told in Snorri Sturluson's (Snorre Sturlasons) Gylfaginning (Gylvaginning).
claims.statement_id: Kisah asal-usul puisi dan mead Suttungr diceritakan dalam Gylfaginning (Gylvaginning) karya Snorri Sturluson (Snorre Sturlasons).
claims.quote: Historien om opphavet til skaldskapen og Suttungs mjød er fortalt i Snorre Sturlasons Gylvaginning.

claims.statement: The Geldmännlein is a kobold-like being of 'lower mythology', a house spirit that provides its owner with money; not always a little man, it may appear as a toad, frog, owl, eagle, worm or beetle.
claims.statement_id: Geldmännlein adalah makhluk mirip kobold dalam "mitologi rendah", roh rumah yang memasok uang bagi pemiliknya; tak selalu berwujud lelaki kecil, ia bisa tampil sebagai kodok, katak, burung hantu, elang, cacing, atau kumbang.
claims.quote: Das Geldmännlein ist ein koboldartiges Wesen der „Niederen Mythologie“, ein Hausgeist, der seinen Eigentümer mit Geld versorgt. Nicht immer hat es die Gestalt eines kleinen Männchens, sondern kann auch als Tier erscheinen, wie z. B. als Kröte oder Frosch, oder als ein Vogel, wie Eule oder Adler, gelegentlich als Wurm oder Käfer.

claims.statement: Closely related is the legend of the Drak as a fiery dragon; similar motifs appear in the tale of the gold donkey and the goose that lays golden eggs, and it shades into human-like root figures such as the Alraune.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Drak dalam wujud naga api berkerabat dekat; motif serupa ada dalam dongeng keledai emas dan angsa bertelur emas, dan peralihannya ke sosok mirip manusia dari akar seperti Alraune berlangsung mulus.
claims.quote: Nah verwandt ist die Sage vom Drak in Gestalt eines feurigen Drachens. Ähnliche Motive finden sich im Märchen vom Goldesel und der Fabel von der Gans, die goldene Eier legt. Fließend ist der Übergang zu menschenähnlichen Figuren, die man aus Wurzeln, wie der Alraune, herstellt

claims.statement: The first mention by name is in 1657 court records against Caspar Michel Fuchs of Sulzfeld near Meiningen, accused of owning a geldtmännlein.
claims.statement_id: Penyebutan pertama dengan nama ini terdapat pada 1657 dalam berkas pengadilan terhadap Caspar Michel Fuchs dari Sulzfeld dekat Meiningen, yang dituduh memiliki geldtmännlein.
claims.quote: Die erste namentliche Erwähnung findet sich 1657 in den Gerichtsakten gegen einen Caspar Michel Fuchs aus Sulzfeld im Grabfeld bei Meiningen, der beschuldigt wurde, ein geldtmännlein zu besitzen.

claims.statement: The Geldmännlein was kept in a chest, box or pot where money was put in the evening; next morning the 'hatched' money was taken out, never all, so the rest could multiply; like other house spirits it got offerings of milk, bread or porridge.
claims.statement_id: Geldmännlein disimpan dalam peti, kotak, atau periuk tempat uang diletakkan pada malam hari; paginya uang yang "dierami" diambil, tetapi tak pernah semuanya agar sisanya terus berlipat; seperti roh rumah lain ia diberi sesaji susu, roti, atau bubur.
claims.quote: Das Geldmännlein befand sich, je nach Gestalt und Größe, in einer Kiste, einer Schachtel oder einem Topf, in welche man am Abend Geld legte. Am nächsten Morgen nahm man das „ausgebrütete“ Geld heraus, aber niemals alles, damit sich der Rest weiter vermehren konnte. Wie anderen Hausgeistern wurden dem Geldmännlein Speiseopfer dargebracht, wie Milch, Brot oder Brei.

claims.statement: Martin Luther in his Tischreden already mentioned a peasant woman suspected of having a Heckergroschen (breeding coin).
claims.statement_id: Martin Luther dalam Tischreden-nya sudah menyebut seorang petani perempuan yang dicurigai memiliki Heckergroschen (uang pelipat).
claims.quote: Aber schon Martin Luther erwähnte in seinen Tischreden eine Bäuerin, die man verdächtigte, einen Heckergroschen zu haben.

claims.statement: It is also called Heckemännchen, Geldschisser or Geldbrüter.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga disebut Heckemännchen, Geldschisser, atau Geldbrüter.
claims.quote: Je také nazýván také Heckemännchen „mužíček živého plotu“, Geldschisser „peníze kálející“ či Geldbrüter „peníze rodící“.

claims.statement: It looks like a little grey man, sometimes with a red cap and green vest, and sometimes turns into animals such as a frog, toad, owl or beetle.
claims.statement_id: Ia berwujud lelaki kecil kelabu, kadang bertopi merah dan berompi hijau, dan kadang berubah menjadi hewan seperti katak, kodok, burung hantu, atau kumbang.
claims.quote: Má podobu šedivého mužíčka, někdy s červenou čapkou a zelenou vestou, a někdy se mění ve zvířata – žábu, ropuchu, sovu či brouka.

claims.statement: Unlike the Drac (draca), it is almost impossible to get rid of: the first two owners may sell it, but the third owner's soul falls to hell.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dengan Drac (draca), Geldmännlein hampir mustahil disingkirkan: dua pemilik pertama boleh menjualnya, tetapi jiwa pemilik ketiga jatuh ke neraka.
claims.quote: Na rozdíl od draca jej téměř nemožné se jej zbavit, první dva majitelé jej mohou prodat, ale duše třetího propadne peklu.

claims.statement: Names vary by region: Geldmännlein is typical of Saxony (Sasko) and Thuringia (Durynsko), Geldschisser of Bavaria (Bavorsko), Alraunel of Lower Austria (Dolní Rakousy).
claims.statement_id: Sebutannya berbeda menurut daerah: Geldmännlein khas di Sachsen (Sasko) dan Thüringen (Durynsko), Geldschisser di Bayern (Bavorsko), Alraunel di Austria Hilir (Dolní Rakousy).
claims.quote: Označení se liší především krajově, Geldmännlein je typický pro Sasko a Durynsko, Geldschisser pro Bavorsko, Alraunel pro Dolní Rakousy.

claims.statement: If the food did not please it, it could grow angry and take revenge.
claims.statement_id: Bila makanannya tak berkenan, ia bisa marah dan membalas dendam.
claims.quote: Wenn ihm die Speisen nicht zusagten, konnte es zornig werden und sich rächen.

claims.statement: Luther was utterly opposed to such folk belief.
claims.statement_id: Luther sangat menolak kepercayaan rakyat semacam itu.
claims.quote: Luther stand solchem Volksglauben äußerst ablehnend gegenüber

claims.statement: In German (německém) folklore the Geldmännlein ('little money man') is a being or magic object that magically brings its owner money.
claims.statement_id: Geldmännlein ("lelaki kecil uang") dalam cerita rakyat Jerman (German; německém) adalah makhluk atau benda ajaib yang secara gaib membawa uang bagi pemiliknya.
claims.quote: Geldmännlein „peněžní mužíček“ je v německém folklóru bytost či kouzelný předmět magicky přinášející svému majiteli peníze.
